chapters.title: Chapter 1520: The Talk (1)
paragraphs: When Kent and Inaya appeared in the harem tower, they didn’t jump into each other’s arms right away.
While it was the most logical decision they could have made, given the state of their relationship the last time they saw each other, they both knew there were some things that had to be said first.
In both a logical and emotional sense, it appeared Jest had abandoned Inaya.
From her perspective, Jest left her for her mortal enemy. Jest was aware of the dynamics between her and that woman, yet he betrayed her with such a vixen.
That is unforgivable.
So while the love he had for her still burned like the morning sun, that soothing warmth wasn’t there for Inaya like she would have loved.
In her mind, Jest abandoned her, so that had to be cleared out of the way first.
However, before any of that, Kent took her around the Love Garden, introducing her to the beautiful surroundings.

There may have been some hatred in Inaya’s heart toward him; however, the beauty of the harem tower wasn’t something she could frown upon, not when, deep in her heart, she was still that loving lady who suppressed the hatred in her heart to find love.
They walked around for half an hour before arriving at the Love Pool.
They removed their footwear and sat on the edge, sinking their feet into the cold water. They remained in that state for five good minutes before Inaya finally asked the question.
"What happened, Jest?" she turned and looked at him. "You told me to wait for you, and I did, but you never came. Why?"
Kent sighed, knowing the reason would take more than a few words to fully explain—at least that would have been the case if this were him, with memories of only his life as Jest.
Thankfully, he had Chaos memories too, so he knew the source of it all. This narrowed down his words. However, it was still a lot to say, and a bit difficult to say... unless.
"Before I tell you what happened, I have a very important question, and your answer will determine what I can say and what I can’t."
Inaya looked at him for a few seconds before nodding.
Kent took a deep breath and then spoke the words Inaya never planned on hearing this early... "Will you marry me?"
"Huh..." Her eyes widened, disbelief appearing on her face. She blanked out instantly.
Kent smiled and shook his head. "Will you marry me, Inaya? I know it is sudden, but before anything, I want to know."
Many thoughts ran through Inaya, causing her to sigh a few times. Before they parted ways, they indeed had plans to marry in a grand wedding.
While their reputation as the Blood Sword couple made them enemies of many swordsmen, they also had many friends they wanted to invite to the wedding.
However, that never happened, and after billions of years apart, the same magical words were asked again.
She didn’t know what to say. Well, she knew what she wanted to say; it was just that she never expected herself to say it.
In the end, she said it, a sigh escaping her lips afterwards...
"Yes."
Kent smiled and gave the Tower the signal to add her to the harem. In no time, Inaya felt the connection form between them. This made her look at Kent with a suspicious gaze.
"It is a long story, one that I will tell you soon. But first, let’s focus on what happened back then."
She nodded, and Kent started to speak.
"It all started during the Primordial Era, when I was known by all as the Primordial Chaos Dragon."

"Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. Before it all began, I was called Chaos, a dragon born from a lone egg. Later, after some not-so-easy decisions were made, I died and reincarnated as a slave who aspired to be free and roam the universe, fighting one swordsman after another.
After years of longing, he indeed gained his freedom, and so he embarked on his quest to become the greatest swordsman to ever live.
He achieved his dream, but at the cost of his love and happiness." Kent paused and looked at the small brown cloud forming in the sky.

"I never planned to abandon you, Inaya. I did so because I found out that coming to you would be the end of you and our unborn children. I was destined to have two children with you, live a happy life, and raise our children into amazing warriors.
However, in the end, I was meant to kill you all. I was meant to kill all three of you with my bare hands, and the reason for that was due to the heart demon I developed during the Primordial Era."
Dia’s image appeared in Inaya’s head. "Does this have anything to do with Dia?"

Kent nodded. "Yes. However, the whole story involves Unity. You see, during the Primordial Era, I had this one friend who fell in love with me at first sight. It is a bit weird, considering the first time we met, I killed her teammates in the most brutal way possible.
However, she fell in love with me, and while I never knew what love was, she tried to teach me. Long story short, I failed to realise that until it was too late.
After her death, I became crazy and burned with the passion for revenge, so I did. I let go of everything she taught me, and for years, I embarked on a chilling journey of slaughter and bloodshed.

Along the way, I caught sight of a young archer. She was the light of her family and everyone she met. She was destined for greatness, fated to be someone worthy of her name. However, she abandoned everything and started following me.

I knew she was following me, but I never tried to make her feel at home until her last moment. I was filled with so much hatred that I failed to see that her friendship was what I needed at that moment.

After she died, I did what I always do best: I avenged her. However, her big sister, for reasons I didn’t know until today, blamed me for her death. She, of course, wasn’t wrong. Artemis died because of me, so I was to blame.
However, the hatred toward me grew to the point that she became someone else entirely. Later, when I met her, we fought, and in the end, I had no choice but to end her misery.
However, by killing her, I invoked a curse in the form of a heart demon that would hunt me down for the rest of my very long lives.

That was why, during the divine era, after I returned from my last search and found nothing that would help me find a path to the Sword Celestial stage, I gave up and chose to come to you as I promised.
I planned to build a family with you as we planned. I planned to hold a grand wedding like you wanted, inviting all our friends and enemies alike.
I even planned to invite the Grim Blade Supreme and use the cover of our wedding to secretly kill him.

However, on my way to Planet Genesis, I met her. They called her the Horror of the stars back then. Of course, I didn’t know who or what she was, so we fought for several months. In the end, after I managed to suppress her, I discovered her true nature.
She was my heart demon, something that came as a shock to me, yet I completely believed her.

After all, I felt it deep within me and knew, with every fibre of my being, that if I went against what she showed me and came to you, the perfect family we would have built would have been destroyed by me, no thanks to my insidious heart demon."

chapters.title: Chapter 1521: The Talk (2)
paragraphs: "I saw two visions. One showed me a happy family. We had two children—a male and a female. We watched them grow up, and just when we were at the peak of happiness, I woke up to the sight of all three of you dismembered by my own bloody hands.

The second vision showed me abandoning you. After I did, you were heartbroken. You felt betrayed, but on top of all that, you still loved me. That was, of course, a problem because I discovered that the longer you loved me, the danger would always loom over your head.
It would get to the point where you would choose to become strong enough to find me and tell me your mind. That would lead you to take the Supreme Tribulation, which would have been your death.
Every route led to your death, so I created a different ending.
I turned and left, later using everything at my disposal to make you hate me." Kent sighed, a bit regretful now that he had said it out loud.
"I knew that since you had cultivated the Ten Emotion Sword Dao, getting you to hate me would be simple. I merely had to pull the right string, and so I chose to..."
"Mess around with that bitch."
Kent turned and looked at Inaya oddly. "She is your sister, Inaya."
"It changes nothing. The next time I see her, I will probably kill her for taking my man and killing my favourite sister."

"She didn’t, Inaya. I told her what happened and what would happen to you if I returned to your side. Knowing your fate, she didn’t hesitate to play along, knowing full well you would hate her even more."
"Then I will cut off one ear and an arm the next time I see her."
Kent laughed.
Had it not been for witnessing what happened to Dia and the fact that Kent is a dragon, it would have been hard for her to accept anything Kent had just said.

In fact, it sounded even more ridiculous now that she had time to think it over. However, deep down, she knew he was telling the truth, and an even more humbling fact was that she would have done the same thing if she were in Jest’s shoes.
However, it pained her heart to learn that the only way to be safe was to hate the one person she swore to love till the end.
All Jest did was make an impossible choice. But when it came to her turn, her hatred for Jest ignited, and now that she stood alive and well, her heart started to break all over again.

Kent knew what was going on in her mind, so he just took her hand and gave it a gentle squeeze. "It was the only way, Inaya. I made sure you hated me by pulling on the only vulnerability you had. However, now that you are alive and by my side again, you don’t have to blame yourself.
Rather, be happy. Don’t let the past ruin the beautiful future ahead of us."
She nodded, her other hand moving toward her chest. A few seconds later, she sighed, then a smile formed on her face...
"I am sorry for doubting you, Jest. I shouldn’t have jumped to conclusions back then."
Kent said nothing, but he nodded.
He also sensed it.
Something was changing within Inaya as they spoke. It wouldn’t manifest for a few months; however, he could tell she was slowly breaking through the barrier between the God and the Supreme stage.
In other words, she would soon transcend beyond godhood, finally stepping into the ranks of Supremacy.
Due to her heartbreak back then, she developed a heart demon that prevented her from advancing to the Supreme stage. But that heart demon was dying, freeing her stagnated cultivation base.
"So how did you finally figure it out?" Inaya asked. "You know, finally becoming a Sword Celestial?"

Kent smiled. "I created a sword technique that surpassed the Sword Supreme stage. Once that happened, I realised it wasn’t that there was no path to the peak of swordsmanship; it was just that someone or something blocked it.
So I did what I do best and severed it clean in half. Once that was accomplished, the path opened for me and others who came after me."
Inaya looked at his handsome face for a few seconds before she smiled. "You are a monster, Jest."
She leaned in and kissed him. "I am still pissed at you, but as someone who walked the path of the sword with you, I want to congratulate you, even if it is several eras too late."𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦
She leaned in and kissed him again. This time, it took some time before she pulled back. A small red tint appeared on her cheeks.
While it was a bit too late for all this, she indeed was happy for him. She never had the chance to do that, since Jest was nowhere to be found back then.

She had always supported him in his quest to reach the peak of swordsmanship. When they both became Sword Supremes, she stood by his side for 400,000 years, searching tirelessly for a path that led to the peak.

So there was just this wave of joy she always felt whenever she remembered the day she heard that Jest had reached the peak. That day, she cried heavy tears, for she wasn’t there to celebrate with him.
Reminiscing about the past had, in a way, brought it back. However, being held by Kent, she seemed to have calmed down a bit.
They remained in silence for a few minutes before Inaya suddenly asked... "So how did you die...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1522: Lord Genesis Final Moments
paragraphs: Kent precisely recalled to Inaya what happened in his final moments during the divine era.

"During the last moments of the Divine War, one of the Sword Elders discovered the source of the breach, and so I, along with all twelve Sword Elders, ventured there against all odds, knowing that once the guardian of the gate was cut down, the invasion would end.
It took us two years to get there because of the dangers we faced along the way. When we finally came face to face with the guardian, I was given the fright of my life."
Kent visibly shuddered.
This display told Inaya that what he saw indeed caused him the greatest fear of his life. She could only wonder, since she wasn’t there to witness it herself.
"It turned out that in the Foreign Realm, there are three Kings. They were known as the Kings of Divine Trinity: the Heavens King, the Earth King, and the Abyss King.

The one we went to meet was the Abyss King, a rather terrible individual, if you ask me. We expected there to be dozens of Celestials waiting for us there, but we met only one, and he was stronger than a thousand Celestials combined."
Inaya squinted her eyes—something she loved to do...
"Are you saying what I think you are saying...?"
"Yes, the Abyss King was someone above the rank of a Celestial. Of course, he wasn’t fully above it, more like halfway there."
"How is that even possible?" Inaya was visibly shocked, and given how her chest was heaving, she seemed even more troubled on the inside.
Back when Jest was arguing his case to the twelve Sword Elders, he claimed there was another sword realm above the Sword Supreme stage simply because there is a Celestial stage cultivation realm.
His logic was that simple. Since we have Celestials, there can also be sword Celestials.
His argument was met with considerable criticism; however, he later proved them wrong and helped all twelve of them reach the peak within a few hundred years.
Later, when Jest glimpsed into another realm beyond the Sword Celestial stage, they should have suspected there to be another realm above the Celestial stage.
However, they never did, until it was too late.
"You know, when we discovered this, the only thought that came to mind was greed. I sensed it, and as you are already thinking, so did the other twelve Sword Elders.
Long story short, the Abyss King offered to help them reach his level, and so they accepted his offer in a heartbeat. Those greedy, uncultured, deluded, evil bastards.
In a flash, I went from having twelve Celestials behind me to thirteen powerhouses against me.

I knew I wouldn’t win the battle, so I did the only thing I knew would save this universe and everyone I love. Making sure you were safe from that threat was everything to me. So, I used my life force to push them all back to the Foreign Realm and seal the gate shut.

It was the shortest battle I ever fought, yet the most impactful. I died a few days after, forever lifting the threat of my heart demon off your head and saving the universe in the process."𝙛𝓻𝒆𝒆𝒘𝙚𝓫𝙣𝙤𝒗𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
Inaya looked at him closely once again, and after a few seconds, she hugged him tightly.
There were so many questions she wanted to ask, but hearing how he died, she knew there was nothing more important than holding him right now.

Strangely, as she held him, feeling his breath on her neck, the seal of hatred that had bloomed into a heart demon deep in her heart was being destroyed much faster than she had felt a few minutes ago.
If she was meant to become a Supreme in one year’s time, then that time had been reduced to eight months due to how fast she was being freed.
They remained like that for a few more minutes before they pulled back.
"It wasn’t too terrible, really. I got to see real danger up close and know that when we meet next time, the one who will feel despair will be him.
As for the twelve Sword Elders, for their betrayal, I will happily take my time and kill them all."
The aura of vengeance, something Jest had cultivated over thousands of years of exacting revenge, oozed from Kent’s body, making Inaya smile.
"I have no doubt about that, my love. Only that this time, I will be by your side like it should have been," her hold on him tightened.
"Though, how do you plan on getting rid of your heart demon?" She paused and then added in a chilling tone, "I suppose killing Dia won’t solve it either."
Kent looked at Inaya for a split second before he smirked. As someone who had cultivated the Ten Emotion Sword Dao, she could turn off her empathy like flicking a switch.
If killing Dia would solve the problem, she would have no problem beheading her. It was one reason why it took them a million years to realise their feelings for each other.
Inaya could be considered the incarnation of mood swings.
"No, killing Dia won’t solve anything. In fact, I came to Planet Brymrr to seek your help in permanently eradicating it."
"Then what are you waiting for? Go ahead and tell me what you need."

"The reason why Ainna said my fate is complex is because I have an incomplete fate. The reason, however, had to do with my first incarnation. A few years before I was cursed, a Forsaken Seer saved me despite the hatred I have for her kind.
She bandaged me, cared for me, and when I was healed, she let me leave. This encounter, however, resulted in me unknowingly losing a part of my fate to her.
Later, she was discovered by her people, and they sealed her away in a place only a few had ever returned."
Kent paused and then asked his next question:
"Mind telling me what business you had venturing into Amon’s Guillotine Cave?"

Inaya blinked a few times, then a smile appeared on her face. "I needed a place so quiet and free from the wars of the universe to take a nap, so I chose there as my bedroom for a few eras." She grinned.
"Best four eras of my life."
Kent shook his head, a bit stunned and dumbfounded upon hearing why she ventured into such a harrowing place.

"Well, I need you to go there again and retrieve the Forsaken Seer for me. I don’t know if she was also taking a nap like you, but I need her to hand over the other half of my fate so I can rid myself of this heart demon.
If I can’t do that before I reach godhood, Dia and I will both be in danger."
"Sure. I must become a Supreme first, though. Those bastards in that dreadful place will surely pick a fight, so I better prepare well before going."
"You have two years to prepare, so get on it before I am forced to shove you there myself."
"Oh, confident now, are we not?" Inaya grinned and was about to activate her evil side when Kent grabbed her and pulled both of them into the water.
He moved closer and kissed her. A few kisses underwater later, they surfaced and continued to kiss more.
It had been billions of years, after all; they owed each other a kiss or two.

Even so, Unity is the best person to help her, so she is doing her best.
Aside from that, Velyra had returned to the tower but soon entered her primordial space.
She had absorbed all the blood she took from the Chaos Envoy and advanced from the Heavenly Ascension stage to the Death stage.
This meant that with one more breakthrough, she would become an Immortal.
However, until then, she needed to help her Primordial Spirit reach the Death stage as well, since she planned to advance to the Immortal stage together.
Her sisters are happy for her, and most importantly, they all want her to succeed.
It is not every day one finds a way to break past the limitations of the heavens.
While they had all broken many limits, making them a bit more susceptible to pushing beyond the world’s limits, doing so takes courage and a great deal of time.
So she had accomplished something great.
On the other side, Yi Lai had also welcomed her 8th undead dragon.
The Fallen Immortal that she and her teammates killed managed to pass the Dragon Ascension Trial and came out as an Immortal Emperor.
Naturally, he is now the strongest of her undead.
Fero was the strongest, but now Draxion had taken that title and would be holding it for now until at least one of the three demigods she had been preparing for passed their trials.
Talking about Fero, after spending two months inside an interplanetary ship traveling through a space channel, they finally landed three days ago on Planet Skar.
Avotha, Vargus, Axiom, Kailan, and Fero got to work right away.
They had no time to waste...

chapters.title: Chapter 1526: The Rescue Mission (1)
paragraphs: Planet Skar is a demon-dominated planet. To the rest of the universe, these demons are called Beast demons. However, on Planet Skar, they are categorized into three groups: the redhorn demons, greenhorn demons, and blackhorn demons.
This naming was due to the color of their horns.

The planet has a red sun and a red moon, so the clouds are crimson at all times. In the morning, the sky is illuminated by the bleeding crimson of the day sun, and now the ever-crimson moon graces the sky with its chilling yet pleasant hue.
Due to the redness at all times, the planet has an air of danger to it.
Though it is widely known that demons are a race of chaotic, evil beings, not every demon is a danger to society. Some actually have gentle hearts.
This planet may have an ominous atmosphere; however, that doesn’t change the fact that not all of them are a danger.
It has three continents, each ruled by a Demon King. On each continent, there are warlords, with Warlord Biana on the Grave Continent.
The Grave Continent is home to the blackhorn demons. It is also the place where the mission will take place.
Their mission is to rescue the Princess of the Green-skinned Rabbit race.
She had been kidnapped by a Soul Temple agent and sold to Warlord Biana. So they are there to rescue her and, if possible, kill the warlord.
Three days ago, Vargus and his teammates landed on this continent and spread out to gather intelligence.

Three days later, inside an inn, Avotha, Vargus, Fero, Axiom, and Kailan gathered around a table to reveal what they had been able to gather. If it was enough to go on, then tomorrow, they would make their move.
Vargus took a large gulp of the ale in his cup and smiled. "Good wine."
He smiled and turned to face his teammates. "Can we stay here a few more days after we kill that bitch?"
"Why not?" Axiom smiled and nodded. "Though killing the warlord will be a bit tricky. From what I have gathered about her, she indeed has the princess as her slave. She is one of her main maids.

To get to her, however, we have to move through the inner part of her base, which has been reinforced by a Tier 26 Killing Formation. It will trigger the moment it senses an unfamiliar hostile aura, so regardless of how careful we are, it will activate the moment we make our move.

I calculate a 20% chance we can leave before it traps us. However, that will depend on two things: whether we can rescue the princess and take her into the tower before her master notices her disappearance."
Axiom paused for a sip of his wine and then continued:
"That would be impossible because even if we manage to take her away, the slave collar around her neck has been rigged to explode after moving some distance from her master.
So, regardless of how fast we try to remove it, we won’t be fast enough.
This leaves us with only one way to go, and that is to kill the warlord first. I can get us in undetected, but getting to her residence will be a bit tricky.
But even if we get to her, how sure are we that we can kill her fast enough? I may not be speaking nonsense here, but I believe she is stronger than a demigod."
Avotha nodded. "She is indeed stronger than a demigod. In fact, she is a pseudo-god. This is why killing her easily, as we had hoped, will be a bit of a problem.

Of course, I can take her on alone. But it will take some time to kill her, so we would have to rule out a silent battle. So, from the way I see it, we would be going in hot, raining down fire in their head. This then means that we will be facing more opponents than we planned for.
We will also have to be ready to handle the killing formation.

Aside from that, she has two immediate subordinates who are demigods, not any weaker than the average demigod. Then there are the twelve Immortal Lords, who would undoubtedly reveal themselves the moment the battle starts. The rest are numerous but weaklings from my perspective.
We can try assassinating them before getting to the main target. Once they are taken off the map, we can move in and face the warlord, her two demigod guards, and the 12 immortal lords.
However, there is one little issue that will prevent us from succeeding in our assassination."
"The formation," Fero muttered.
"Indeed. It would activate the moment the first target is assassinated. This means aside from the warlord, the next dreadful obstacle is the formation."

Avotha took a sip of his wine and let a faint smile appear on his lips. "But it would be fun. Going into battle knowing full well the odds are stacked against you, yet you have no reason to retreat...from my perspective, it feels like the life we ought to lust after."
Avotha is a bit crazy, which, from how it seems, Vargus and Axiom are on the same level of craziness as him. Hearing his words, they grin. Only Kailan and Fero shook their head in disbelief.
Then again, they are only the True Immortal and an Immortal King. They have no business stacking odds.
Avotha smiled and put out his plan, "I will take on the Warlord, while Vargus goes for the two demigods. Axiom and Kailan will handle the twelve Immortal Lords, while Fero will handle the formation."
"There is a chance we will die and end up in hell. However, as a sworn brother to one of the Kings of Hell, I am not afraid at all."
Vargus replied, "My big brother is the overlord of all of hell, so I am covered as well."
Fero, who hadn’t known these bastards for long, turned and looked at Axiom and Kailan. "What about you two? Any plans in the event you end up dead all of a sudden?"

"Not really," Axiom replied. "Though I felt insulted that Avotha assumed we are only qualified to fight Immortal Lords. If anything, taking on the demigods would pose a challenge we would love to face."

Kailan took over. "You would do well to know that during the Primordial Era, whenever we arrived on battlefields, the enemies ran like chickens. So no, we have no fear of dying...but even if we were to end up dead, we wouldn’t feel anything since we don’t have emotions nor feel pain."

"Very chilling, guys. But as you all know, I am a dragon, and as a dragon, I don’t see myself on the level of these lower existences. If my mission is to handle the formation, be sure to get your jobs done by the time I destroy the formation. You wouldn’t want me looking down on you all."
In what may sound like the most arrogant thing ever said, Fero made it seem like he would be doing the most difficult part of the job. There is a chance he might even fail...
While that is true, the fact that he claims to be a higher existence makes Avotha, who is also a dragon, smirk. They are both dragons, but he doesn’t walk around looking down on everyone.
"Just don’t die. The formation can kill a demigod and wound a god, so if you can’t handle it, don’t get close."
"I will be fine."
Everyone nodded. The mission is a dangerous one, perhaps the deadliest they would face for a while. However, Avotha is someone who can challenge even an early god.
Killing the warlord is within his reach. How fast he can do it, however, depends on how quickly he gains the advantage.

"We attack tomorrow at sunrise," Avotha declared. "Vargus and I will force our way in. That will bring out the warlord and her immediate generals. Once we engage them, Axiom, you will make your appearance by taking out as many demons as you can. Kailan will follow.

By then, the formation will activate, which will be the perfect time for Fero to join in the fun. Now, I want to stress that the mission is to rescue the princess, so if we manage to deactivate her slave collar, we should retreat to the tower.
We can come back later and finish off the warlord."
"Sounds like a plan," Fero responded after listening to Avotha’s plan.
"I am ready to rock and roll," Axiom nodded.
"Killing a demigod will make me happy at least," Vargus, who was already prepared to unleash flame and axe on everyone, beat his chest, causing a wave of energy to spread through the inn.
His friends gave him smug looks and smiled faintly at the people who turned to look.

While Avotha and his friends were finalizing their plan, a redheaded dragon man sat behind a table, a flame-infused wine releasing waves of steam from his glass as he looked out the window, staring at a black mansion not far from him.
After looking for a few minutes, he turned away, took a sip of his drink, and sighed, "Won’t be long now."

chapters.title: Chapter 1527: The Rescue Mission (2)
paragraphs: The Silent Graves is a mercenary team led by the great Warlord Biana.
Over the last thousand years, they had dominated the Grave Continent and a few wastelands on Planet Skar, amassing great wealth and power.

Their reputation for brutality and slaughter had been registered in everyone’s mind, so people knew better than to antagonize any of their members. Members from that dreadful team do as they please, knowing full well nobody would dare mess with them.
Today, one of the members was celebrating his birthday, so everyone was in a festive mood.
They, of course, never expected their cheerful atmosphere to soon turn into a chaotic mess, one that would send ripples spreading all over Planet Skar and beyond.

"Nire, since today is your 3,090th birthday, allow me to make a toast to your short life. You are the youngest of us, but you have done so much to earn your place. Ten years from today, I want to see you even stronger and more powerful than you are now. To Nire."
"To Nire," everyone cheered and started to drink to their fill.
As the mood grew even more pleasant, more booze was brought out, adding to the cheers. They drank to their fill and had the best time of their lives.
As if by design, they managed to fully celebrate Nire’s birthday and even made plans for the next time one of them would also celebrate their own.

Given how much the lifespan increases as one ascends in cultivation, celebrating birthdays every year is meaningless. The younger ones do so every 10 years, while those who have lived for 10,000 years or more do so every 100 years.
Some even do so every few thousand years, with the old bags of bones going millions of years without celebrating their birthdays.
So while there are many mercenaries with their birthdays coming up soon, they wouldn’t celebrate until a couple more years have passed.
Eventually, the celebration came to an end, and many retired to their homes.
Soon, however, their worst fear arrived.
The atmosphere at the Silent Graves was calm until a large shadow enveloped the space, dark clouds forming overhead.
Before many could rise from their beds to see what was happening, a terrible pressure descended on them, accompanied by a chilling voice.

"I don’t suppose anyone knows where I can find the bitch who calls herself Biana," Avotha’s voice filled the camp of the Silent Graves, with thousands losing consciousness, the weaker ones dying in the process.
He was in his human form, but even his terrible power was enough to send Immortal Lords to their knees. Some even lost their balance in the most unexpected moments, breaking a few bones.
However, the pressure was lifted when a furious tone came from a stony mansion not far from Avotha.
"Who dares break into my domain?"
Underground, a formation activated, and arrays started rising into the air.

Warlord Biana appeared, her hand gripping a black spear with a red, razor-sharp tip. She had short, dark hair and an athletic build that suggested she was both nimble like a cat and flexible like an assassin.
The aura around her was subtle, a bit calm for someone who looked both furious and enraged.
"So you are the one called Biana." Avotha extended his hand and gave her a thumbs-down. "I expected better."
This gesture caused the expression on Warlord Biana’s face to harden. However, before she could have the time to become more furious, the battle began.
Avotha moved, and Warlord Biana’s eyes widened.
Before she could react to the sudden movement, a terrible punch landed on her left breast, sending her crashing into a mountain 300 meters away, a piercing scream of pain escaping her lips.
"That’s for enslaving a princess," the Death Dragon said.
He took one step and stood before Biana, whose expression darkened as a violet aura oozed from her body. Two black horns appeared on her forehead.
Avotha clenched his fist and was about to land another punch when the void exploded from behind him, two weapons—a sword and a scythe—piercing through its dark maw.
Their tips gleam with deadly intent, both weapons aimed to claim his life.
He turned sideways and was about to block when a great axe bathed in green flames came from the other direction and clashed into them.
This allowed Avotha to land his blow. Unfortunately, Biana used the momentary distraction to defend, blocking the punch with her spear.
The impact, however, sent her staggering back a few more meters.
At the same time, two demigods appeared from the void and were about to speed toward their mistress’s rescue when Vargus landed, creating a terrifying shockwave.
"Kindly entertain me, please." He extended his large arm, and his axe flew into it.
Then, with a heavy step, he was upon the two demigods, who knew it would be a while before they could get to their leader—that is, if they themselves managed to survive.
Their battle soon began, creating chaos everywhere.
The immortals were left stunned, unsure of what to do. The scale of the battle wasn’t one they were qualified to fight in. In fact, they ran the risk of death if they remained where they were.
Some began to retreat, while others, tapping into their sense of duty and blind loyalty, chose to remain and look for ways to interfere in the battles to give their side an advantage.

That thought soon changed when, all of a sudden, strings came out of nowhere and latched onto over a hundred immortals. Before any of them could react, they were pulled into the void, vanishing forever.
"Run and live, stay and die."
Kailan burst out from the void, and his massacre began. He wielded his spear with deadly might, cleaving through one immortal after another.

The formation came to life, but it was quickly discovered that it wasn’t all-knowing. In fact, the moment it activated, it tried to lock onto Avotha, but with how fast he was moving, it failed. The same was true for Vargus and Kailan.
Axiom was hidden in the void, using its insidious power to trap and pull the immortals inside, never to be seen or heard from again.

Because of this, Fero also joined the battle. The infamous formation was useless, failing to target anyone. He also saw that he was powerless to stop it, so, taking into account what Avotha said, he decided to join Kailan in fighting the immortals.
Unfortunately for them, the formation soon found its target and locked onto him.
Vargus was pushed back by one of the demigods he was fighting. This caused him to slow down a bit, but that was all the time the formation needed.
It locked onto him, and a beam formed. However, it never got to fire in that instant. If it did, it would have missed.
It did, however, slow Vargus down long enough for the spear of one of the demigods to pierce his chest. That injury slowed him down further.

However, he managed to evade the attack from the second demigod, causing her scythe to graze his chest. He jumped back, and when he was about to unleash an overhead swinging slash, a deadly eye locked onto his body.
This move brought him to a near halt.
The formation finally found its death mark, unleashing a blinding beam that sent the surrounding buildings exploding into ruins.

Fero, who was assigned to the formation, knew that even if he were a demigod, that beam wasn’t something he could handle—not when the flame law contained within that beam wasn’t something he could withstand.
In fact, Avotha was also forced to turn and look, giving Biana the chance to attack him.
He didn’t mind the pain.

Instead, three Death Tattoos glowed on his left arm, and he was about to take an impossible gamble when a redheaded demi-dragon appeared before Vargus and extended his hand, using it to block the beam.
The beam that would have incinerated Vargus was blocked, and not even a burn mark was left on his arm.
When the smoke cleared, the redheaded demi-dragon turned and looked to his left and spoke in a disdainful tone:
"Are you going to come out and play, or hide in the clouds like the coward you are,"

Axiom was hidden in the void, using its insidious power to trap and pull the immortals inside, never to be seen or heard from again.
Because of this, Fero also joined the battle.
The infamous formation was useless, failing to target anyone.
He also saw that he was powerless to stop it, so, taking into account what Avotha said, he decided to join Kailan in fighting the immortals.
Unfortunately for them, the formation soon found its target and locked onto him.
Vargus was pushed back by one of the demigods he was fighting.
This caused him to slow down a bit, but that was all the time the formation needed.
It locked onto him, and a beam formed.
However, it never got to fire in that instant.
If it did, it would have missed.
It did, however, slow Vargus down long enough for the spear of one of the demigods to pierce his chest.
That injury slowed him down further.
However, he managed to evade the attack from the second demigod, causing her scythe to graze his chest.
He jumped back, and when he was about to unleash an overhead swinging slash, a deadly eye locked onto his body.
This move brought him to a near halt.
The formation finally found its death mark, unleashing a blinding beam that sent the surrounding buildings exploding into ruins.

Fero, who was assigned to the formation, knew that even if he were a demigod, that beam wasn’t something he could handle—not when the flame law contained within that beam wasn’t something he could withstand.
In fact, Avotha was also forced to turn and look, giving Biana the chance to attack him.
He didn’t mind the pain.

Instead, three Death Tattoos glowed on his left arm, and he was about to take an impossible gamble when a redheaded demi-dragon appeared before Vargus and extended his hand, using it to block the beam.
The beam that would have incinerated Vargus was blocked, and not even a burn mark was left on his arm.
When the smoke cleared, the redheaded demi-dragon turned and looked to his left and spoke in a disdainful tone:
"Are you going to come out and play, or hide in the clouds like the coward you are,"

chapters.title: Chapter 1528: Unexpected Ally
paragraphs: [Ten Minutes Before the Attack on the Silent Graves]
The redheaded dragon man remained seated in the same spot, drinking his hell wine all night long. From time to time, he would look at the black mansion only 5 km away and smirk.
It appeared he harbored some animosity toward someone living there.

However, looking at the strength of the guards stationed around it, he seemed to hesitate from going there. He is only an Immortal Monarch, so facing several Immortal Lords and a few demigods wasn’t something he planned to do.

A few seconds before Avotha and his people attacked the base just 10 km from the black mansion, another figure, shrouded in darkness, emerged from the redheaded dragon man’s shadow and whispered in his ear.
’It is done.’
Nobody inside the inn seemed to sense the person. However, if one did and looked closely, they would see that the person is a demigod.
The redheaded dragon man nodded and was about to take a sip of his wine when a loud boom echoed, spreading out from the base of the Silent Graves.

He shifted his attention over there, and just when he was about to stand up, he turned back to the black mansion. There, a man clad in a black cloak appeared in the air, flew up, and vanished into the clouds.
’Change of plans, Daliah. You have to hold back his guards. I will handle him myself.’
’Are you sure, my lord?’ the figure shrouded in darkness asked, and the redheaded dragon man nodded.
’Do not worry. I wasn’t known as the Primordial Flame King, rival of the Primordial Chaos Dragon, for nothing.’
’He defeated you, though... 30 times, but who is counting?’

The dragon man turned and looked at his shadow. ’Whose side are you on, Daliah? And in case you are not aware, the first time we met, I defeated him.’ He gulped down the last of his hell wine and stood up.
’You know what, why even explain myself?’ He turned into a streak of red light and vanished.
The person in the darkness smirked. ’Only because he had less than 20% of his energy left, and you had all 24 of us to count on. But who is counting?’

The darkness vanished, and soon, the black mansion was covered in absolute darkness. If someone who had mastered the laws of darkness were to be present, they would know this person had reached the Extreme stage.
Their understanding had long since transcended the Absolute stage and entered the realm of Extreme Darkness. So the moment the darkness spread, not even the strongest demigod could escape it.
Meanwhile, when the dragon man left, he appeared somewhere in the camp of the Silent Graves and observed what was happening.
On one side, he saw a dark-haired demigod dragon clashing with Warlord Biana. Looking at how that fight was progressing, the man seemed to have the upper hand.
He was a bit intrigued when he saw the man was just like him—a dragon who doesn’t take anything seriously.
Turning to another side, he saw another brute wielding a green flaming axe, each strike causing the very ground to shake and crack.
Then he turned to another human-looking man who wielded a spear, moving like the wind, killing as he passed.
There was another dragon fighting alongside the spearman. However, he saw that this dragon was also paying attention to the formation that was trying to find a target.
Suddenly, his gaze turned to the brute, who was pushed back, and then, before he could move, a spear was stabbed into his chest.
But that didn’t end there. Just when the brute was about to counter, a powerful presence fell from the clouds, locking him in place.
This gave the formation enough time to charge a beam and fire.
Turning briefly to look up at the clouds, he moved and appeared before Vargus. Then, with a gentle stretch of his hand, he blocked the beam.
It was so effortless that he felt next to nothing. When it cleared, he looked up and spoke:
"Are you going to come out and play, or hide in the clouds like the coward you are?"
Vargus, who was saved, stomped on the ground, and it cracked. At once, the aura around him thickened, and his presence started to exude more power.
His gaze ignited into green flames, spilling out a dreadful smoky aura. From the crack that had appeared on the ground, a large green axe emerged, bathed in flames.
The moment the axe appeared, a terrible pressure descended on the two demigods. He grabbed the axe while the one he wielded melded into sparks of flame essence.
"Thanks for the assist, Mr Dragon. Let’s have a chat later." With that, he moved and swung his axe...
"Hell Flame Killing Circle"
The ground exploded, and literal hell appeared. Flames fueled by the torment and resentment of haunted souls flared into existence, causing the two demigods to panic and break into a cold sweat.
Vargus wasted no time and lunged at them.

Avotha, who was struck, slid across the ground for a few meters but quickly managed to stabilize himself. Just then, he sensed another pseudo-god descending from the clouds, his arms crossed behind his back, a smirk forming beneath his hood.
When he was low enough, he looked down at the redheaded dragon man and asked:

"All this anger and resentment... have we met before. Granted, I have met many people, and thanks to my stellar reputation, I can boldly say none of them ever came back with murderous intent in their eyes. You, on the other hand, seem to want me dead. Why is that?"
He removed the hood, revealing a tattooed face.
"You aren’t even a demigod. Are you sure you are qualified to challenge me?"

The redheaded dragon man sized the man up for a few seconds before he smirked. "Two years ago, you and three others attacked a dragon enclave, trying to get your hands on a dragon stone. You failed, of course, but your chaos killed three dragon children."
"So you are here for revenge. I see, that makes sense." A grin formed on his face. "I did kill a lot of people."

The redheaded dragon man shook his head and let out a cold smile. "You know what, I initially wanted to have an extended battle with you. However, seeing your smug expression now, I know what I have to do."
He turned and looked toward the black mansion, now shrouded in darkness. "Daliah, you have my permission to kill everyone."
The tattooed man frowned and turned to look in the same direction. When he saw the darkness, a panicked look appeared on his face.𝚏𝕣𝐞𝗲𝐰𝕖𝐛𝐧𝕠𝕧𝚎𝚕.𝐜𝚘𝗺
"NO,"
He was about to move when a terrifying presence descended from the sky, sending him crashing to the ground. The dragon man smiled and took one step forward...
"You know, in the past, I was called the Flame King. Back then, many feared me, and so they worshipped me. Why antagonize the devil if you can make him feel special?
I like to be feared, to be worshipped, to be praised by all. Those who failed to do that met my fury. I burned them to a crisp and spat on their ashes.
My presence was divine, godlike if you will. Legendary cultivators run when they sense my presence. Kingdoms bowed their heads in servitude while empires lay down their weapons at my merciful feet.
It was the man, the dragon, the flame king.
I had the power, the fame, and the wealth... I was on top of the world, the universe even. It had it all. That was until I met him, the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
He was aloof, cold, and hated people. In his eyes, people are the worst kind of evil. However, he fought to protect them. He faced harrowing dangers just to keep them safe.
You can say he hated them yet protected them.
In a way, he was the direct opposite of me. That was also why we became rivals the moment we set eyes on each other. My beliefs were what he opposed, and his were opposed to mine.
We clashed thousands of times, each battle more intense than the last.
Years later, we fought side by side, dying while saving him. I regretted nothing because I died for a just cause—the irony in that.

Fate gave me a second chance, and this time, I aspire to be like my rival. I aspire to live like the Primordial Chaos Dragon. I pledge to live like him, which is why I can wield his undying power to smite you."
By the time he ended his speech, he was 100 meters away from the tattooed-faced man. The pressure falling on him had become even more terrible now.
Gritting his teeth, the tattooed man asked,
"W-Who are you?"
The dragon man grinned. "Me, I used to be called the Primordial Flame King. But these days, I go by Uncle Drake."
He raised his hand and spoke the undying words of the Primordial Chaos Dragon.

chapters.title: Chapter 1529: The Chaos Dragon Authority
paragraphs: Lightning churns in the sky, the clouds turning from crimson to dark. At once, the pressure on the tattooed-faced man multiplied, causing him to grit his teeth.
Uncle Drake lifted his hand and spoke.

"I stand in the name of justice. By the will of the Primal One—the Undying Dragon—I invoke the ancient decree of the Primordial Chaos Dragon. Grant me your eternal fury, that I may smite my enemy and deliver peace unto the restless dead."
RUMBLE! RUMBLE!! RUMBLE!!!
All over the planet, every living soul raised its head and looked up. Up in the clouds, a terrifying dragon head appeared, just clear enough for its large reddish-gold eyes to gaze down on everyone.
At once, everyone, be it the three kings or the other two warlords, and even some hidden monsters who would put the warlords to shame, dropped to their knees and bowed, fear enveloping them.
Their bodies shook like a massage chair, some even passing out.
Meanwhile, when the colossal dragon head appeared, Uncle Drake looked up and met its gaze. Then, as if reminded of something, he smirked.
The dragon said nothing.
It merely looked down lazily at Uncle Drake and the others before a crack appeared on one of its scales.
Then a small part of it broke off and flew toward Uncle Drake. When it arrived before him, golden flames surrounded it for a moment before it transformed into a dagger.
"Really?" Uncle Drake lifted his head and looked at the dragon. However, sparing him not even a glance, it receded into the clouds, and the pressure it brought vanished.
Uncle Drake sighed and muttered:
"If that was just 5% of your power, I wonder how much you had given to him."
He regarded the dagger for a few seconds before reaching for it. When his palm wrapped around it, a terrifying power surged through his body.
At once, he went from an Immortal Monarch to a demigod, his untamed power surging like a cosmic sea. Though temporary, he now has the power to match the tattooed-faced man.
Talk about him, he seemed to have already recovered when the dragon head left.
He stood up, but instead of attacking, he seemed uneasy about something as he gazed at Uncle Drake. His instinct screamed at him to run, but he knew that would be impossible.
"Hahahahaha... That is what I am talking about," Uncle Drake laughed. Then he turned and looked at the tattooed-faced man.
"You are dead meat." The poor man was too late to raise his defense. His chest was pierced, and before he could make sense of how that happened, his face was slashed by a razor-sharp claw.
Uncle Drake narrowed, flames igniting in his eyes as he pulled out his dagger. Then he attacked again, and yet again the tattooed man failed to block it.
’Just what is happening?’ he said inwardly, his mind failing to comprehend the sheer form of danger he had found himself in.
"AaaaHhhhh!" He screamed when a powerful kick from a foot coated in metallic dragon scales slammed into his balls. He was shot back, crashing through several buildings.
Yet again, Uncle Drake gave him no breather.
Avotha saw this and smiled.
His expression changed, taking on a twisted, evil smile.
"Ah, looks like someone is stealing my thunder." He grinned, and then his clothes transformed, revealing black-and-red metallic armor around his body.
On his forehead, a Death tattoo glowed, and a third eye opened.
"How about I use 60% of my power now?" He moved and appeared overhead of Warlord Biana. Then, with a stomp, his right foot shot at Warlord Biana.
She gritted her teeth and crossed her spear, hoping to block it. Waves of energy swirled around her, reinforcing both her body and spear.
She did block the attack, but the impact created a crater. She wasn’t even done falling when Avotha appeared overhead again.
Another attack from his foot slammed into Warlord Briana, and the crater turned into a deep hole.
They vanished into its dark maw, unsure of who would be emerging alive. Though from the look of things, the Death Dragon Avotha seemed to have the upper hand.
On the outside, Vargus was also teaching his opponents a good lesson. The wound he sustained from the spear healed. Now, however, his opponents were the ones littered with several injuries.
Before, Vargus was merely using a construct of his soul weapon. Now, however, he had manifested the true form of the Great Oblivion Axe.
While it isn’t the same terrifying spear that was personally tempered in the blood of many Celestials, he can harness at least 5% of its true power now.
The two demigods stood no chance against such power, and that was clear from how they were being trashed.
Axiom still hadn’t shown his main body.

However, it now appeared that he had become one with the void. Unfortunately, too, for the immortals around, the reason the Void Beasts were feared was that, as they killed, their hunger to kill more seemed to grow.
Now, the same was happening as Axiom and Kailan slaughtered all around. Kailan’s speed only seems to increase as he moves, killing left, right, and center.
The formation had lost its power, so Fero was locked in as well. Because of the scale of the battle, he transformed into his True Dragon form and locked into a fight with two Immortal Lords.
He personally requested that, so Axiom and Kailan didn’t bother to come to his aid even when he was in danger.

As an undead linked to both the tower and a master, death is really not something he has to fear. But then again, even if he will also die when his master dies, since Yi Lai is linked to Kent and Kent is the master of the tower, she too cannot die unless Kent does.
But even if Kent were to do so, would the tower really die? There is his soul universe too.
In a way, he is an immortal on a different level of madness.
The battle was both chaotic and furious.
Meanwhile, back inside the harem tower, Kent and Inaya were relaxing in a bathtub, playing with each other’s bodies. Kent’s hand was all over Inaya’s breast while she was busy with his dick.
Suddenly, his eyes glowed golden, releasing a strange energy.
He blinked a few times, and then a wave of energy surged from his body. This caught Inaya’s attention, so she turned and looked at him.
"Everything alright?"
Kent didn’t reply. Instead, he remained still for a few moments, almost as if he was recalling something. When he finally blinked, a faint smile formed on his face.
"Oh... So you are back, huh?"
"Who?" Inaya asked, her brow raised.
"A friend of mine who lived during the Primordial Era." He grabbed Inaya by the waist and lifted her out of the tub. "Dress up, we are going somewhere."
Just now, he received a part of his memories that involved his rivalry and eventual friendship with another dragon who was equally terrifying.
During the Primordial Era, for a few million years, he was measured against this dragon. Later, however, Chaos surpassed him, but the gap between them wasn’t that vast.

During the Great War, they fought side by side. Chaos witnessed how his friend fell. Naturally, his death, among others, was what pushed Chaos to use the Spell of Origin as the last-ditch effort to save the universe.
Sensing he was back and had even invoked his name, he knew he had to see him. This also means his pleasure time with Inaya had come to an end.

He had no idea why he invoked his name, but since he did, it meant he had recovered his memories. To be able to invoke his name, he needed to have the mark of Chaos. He gave that mark to him a few minutes before he fell during the Great War.
Inaya nodded and pressed a necklace. Her body was soon clad in a gown that did a good job of showing her curves and holding her breasts in place. Her cleavage glimmered under the dim light.
Kent looked at her and smiled. "Beautiful as ever."
There was no makeup or other accessories; however, her beauty came out flawless.
Walking toward her, he held her by the waist and kissed her. Then they vanished.
The next moment they appeared, the first thing they saw was a brute slashing off the arm of a demigod.
"VARGUS..."

Axiom still hadn’t shown his main body.
However, it now appeared that he had become one with the void.
Unfortunately, too, for the immortals around, the reason the Void Beasts were feared was that, as they killed, their hunger to kill more seemed to grow.
Now, the same was happening as Axiom and Kailan slaughtered all around.
Kailan’s speed only seems to increase as he moves, killing left, right, and center.
The formation had lost its power, so Fero was locked in as well.
Because of the scale of the battle, he transformed into his True Dragon form and locked into a fight with two Immortal Lords.
He personally requested that, so Axiom and Kailan didn’t bother to come to his aid even when he was in danger.
As an undead linked to both the tower and a master, death is really not something he has to fear.
But then again, even if he will also die when his master dies, since Yi Lai is linked to Kent and Kent is the master of the tower, she too cannot die unless Kent does.
But even if Kent were to do so, would the tower really die?
There is his soul universe too.
In a way, he is an immortal on a different level of madness.
The battle was both chaotic and furious.
Meanwhile, back inside the harem tower, Kent and Inaya were relaxing in a bathtub, playing with each other’s bodies.
Kent’s hand was all over Inaya’s breast while she was busy with his dick.
Suddenly, his eyes glowed golden, releasing a strange energy.
He blinked a few times, and then a wave of energy surged from his body.
This caught Inaya’s attention, so she turned and looked at him.
"Everything alright?"
Kent didn’t reply.
Instead, he remained still for a few moments, almost as if he was recalling something.
When he finally blinked, a faint smile formed on his face.
So you are back, huh?"
"Who?" Inaya asked, her brow raised.
"A friend of mine who lived during the Primordial Era." He grabbed Inaya by the waist and lifted her out of the tub.
"Dress up, we are going somewhere."
Just now, he received a part of his memories that involved his rivalry and eventual friendship with another dragon who was equally terrifying.
During the Primordial Era, for a few million years, he was measured against this dragon.
Later, however, Chaos surpassed him, but the gap between them wasn’t that vast.
During the Great War, they fought side by side.
Chaos witnessed how his friend fell.
Naturally, his death, among others, was what pushed Chaos to use the Spell of Origin as the last-ditch effort to save the universe.
Sensing he was back and had even invoked his name, he knew he had to see him.
This also means his pleasure time with Inaya had come to an end.
He had no idea why he invoked his name, but since he did, it meant he had recovered his memories.
To be able to invoke his name, he needed to have the mark of Chaos.
He gave that mark to him a few minutes before he fell during the Great War.
Inaya nodded and pressed a necklace.
Her body was soon clad in a gown that did a good job of showing her curves and holding her breasts in place.
Her cleavage glimmered under the dim light.
Kent looked at her and smiled.
"Beautiful as ever."
There was no makeup or other accessories; however, her beauty came out flawless.
Walking toward her, he held her by the waist and kissed her.
Then they vanished.
The next moment they appeared, the first thing they saw was a brute slashing off the arm of a demigod.
"VARGUS..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1530: Strange Spear
paragraphs: Kent never had the chance to ask about the rest of his legion when he woke up from his coma. The plan was to catch up with them back then; however, that changed when he met Inaya inside the Tower.
He never expected to find her in the tower.

So he didn’t know Avotha, and a few of his legions had embarked on a mission to rescue a princess who had been sold into slavery. This was why he was a bit stunned when he saw Vargus locked in battle against two demigods.
His voice, however, was drowned in the painful cry of the demigod whose arm Vargus had severed.
Inaya turned and looked at him. Then she asked:
"Do you know him?"
"Yes. He is one of my friends." Kent turned and saw that Kailan and Fero were also locked in fierce battle with their opponents. Fero unleashed a powerful dragon tail slash, splitting the void open.
From within, a dragon fang appeared and stabbed at the chest of one of the two Immortal Lords he was fighting.
Black blood oozes from the stab, invoking a painful scream from the Immortal Lord.
Kent smiled and turned to look at an Immortal King whose head was pierced by an invisible rope, only to be dragged into the void the next second.

’That sneaky coward,’ he smiled weakly, knowing Axiom had already created a horrific prison in the void, using it to house the people he was kidnapping. Later, he would apply spices in the form of torture before devouring them.
Kent thought about using their shared connection to call out to him and tell him to eat only half of the immortals. The other half would be used to upgrade his undead.
The sudden explosion in the distance, however, drew his attention, causing him to pause. Extending the Soul Map, he managed to see what was happening there.
Even long before the explosion, he had already sensed a familiar presence coming from that direction.
The moment the soul map covered her range was when he saw the man, whom he had no idea where he had gone all this while.
A few days after Kent and his friend left for the Supreme Immortal Sect, back on Sonox (the medium world where Kent first appeared after his transmigration), Uncle Drake also left.

He said he was heading to a planet far from Sonox, and so he might lose contact with them for a few years. Kent wanted to ask who would become Sonox’s guardian, since that was the job he had given him.
After all, when he helped him transform from a flame drake to a flame dragon, he promised to do him a solid. Leaving without doing even one year of his service was a bit disappointing.
He was, however, surprised to find out Leviathan, the overlord of the Ancient Sea Race, chose to step in for 1,000 years before ascending.
Since then, he and Uncle Drake never spoke.
Today, they met again, only that this time, Uncle Drake wasn’t the same calm dragon he knew. The man had now become someone he recognized from his past life as Chaos.
’Ignarax,’ Kent said inwardly, a faint smile appearing on his face.
"Is he also one of your friends?" Inaya asked with an amused look. Looking at the smile on Kent’s face, she could tell he knew the redhead dragon man, too.
"I do. Though I never expected him to be here." He turned and looked at Inaya. "Have you heard of the Primordial Flame Dragon? He was like a duplicate of the Primordial Chaos Dragon."
Inaya squinted her eyes and looked at Uncle Drake’s back. "Don’t tell me he was that monster."
"In the flesh."

"I see. I guess that explains why he can was holding back a pseudo-god as a pretend demigod." Inaya had been suppressed to the rank of a demigod since they were in an Immortal World. However, even with such strength, she could tell Uncle Drake was not really a demigod.
If anything, the dagger he was wielding possessed the power of a demigod. But if that was the case, how then was his opponent, who had the power of a pseudo-god stage cultivator, bleeding all over?
"Those arrogant Flame Dragons are going to flip if they learn both the Chaos Dragon and Flame Dragon have returned."
"That would indeed be a problem. I guess I’d better hide my true nature for now. Disguising as an Ice Dragon will—"
Kent paused and let a smile appear on his face. "You wouldn’t happen to have heard anything about the Ice Dragon Monarch, would you?"
Inaya shook her head, making Kent sigh. "Then I am good to go."
Inaya wanted to ask why he asked such a question. Her words caught in her throat when something else drew their attention.
The ground suddenly shook, and a large centipede slithered out. Its long, scaly body was marred by several deep wounds.
The length of the centipede alone was over 1.5 km. Such a monstrosity most often happened to be the one to inflict pain and injuries, not the other way around.
So, for it to be gravely wounded and even pushed near death was a bit scary and somewhat intriguing.
It rose into the air and then transformed into a pale, demonic-looking lady wielding a dark spear. Kent raised his brow when his gaze landed on the spear.
Just then, a crazy voice filled with amusement came from the hole the centipede came out of. "I really like it when they struggle, hoping to escape the inevitable."
Avotha appeared, his expression calm. There wasn’t even a single wound on his body. Rather, his sword seemed to have some blood on it, clearly from the injuries inflicted on Warlord Biana.
He pointed his sword at her and asked:
"Ready to surrender and let yourself be cut down, or should we do it the hard way?"
"Die, you crazy bastard." The spear in her hand vibrated. She burns her life force, causing waves of energy to pour into the sword.
Just when her reserve was almost drained, one of the nine runes on the spear lit up.
At once, the air around turned cold. This coldness, however, wasn’t from ice, but from a deadly killing intent, the kind that made even Inaya tremble.
Instinctively, her hold on Kent tightened

Kent, who held a smile on his face when he saw Avotha appear, frowned. Suddenly, however, he felt a bad premonition, so without even knowing how, he appeared before Warlord Biana and grabbed the spear.
"I will be taking that."
He yanked the spear from her hand and was about to teleport away when a net fell from the clouds, aimed to envelop him.
Kent turned sideways and smirked. "Futile attempt that leads to an inevitable end."
His eyes flashed crimson. Then he extended his hand, and Gaap appeared in it. He closed his eyes for a brief moment. When he opened them, a wave of sword intent poured from them.
"Heaven and Earth Cleaver."𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶

He swung his sword, and a thin line fashioned from sword aura flashed out, cleaving through the net. But it didn’t stop there; the attack cut the cloud in half, revealing a green-skinned demon king looking down at him.
He extended his hand, and the attack landed on his palm, exploding in sparks of flame and mists of smoke.
Kent stored away the spear and spun the sword in his hand. He turned and looked at Avotha and smiled before teleporting out of the way for him to land a deadly punch on Biana’s face.
Inaya appeared beside him, and they both turned and looked at the demon king.
"I suppose you aren’t trying to interfere, Your Highness?" Kent asked with a small smirk, before adding, "It would be sad if we had to cross swords knowing it wouldn’t end well for you."
The air hung with anticipation as the two locked in a fierce gaze.
The Demon King, who had lost his only chance to obtain the spear he had been eyeing for years, maintained his murderous gaze on him for a few moments before he teleported away.

chapters.title: Chapter 1531: Reckless Decision
paragraphs: There were a few things that could have gone wrong had Kent not appeared on the battlefield when he did.
The battle, while the Silent Graves were bound to lose, considering Axiom, Kailan, Fero, and Vargus would probably end up killing all of its members, the same could not be said for Avotha.
Physically, he is stronger than Warlord Biana. He has more techniques and an even stronger bloodline than she. However, she had something Avotha would have fallen prey to: her weapon.
The spear she wielded wasn’t an ordinary weapon. In fact, it is quite dangerous to both Avotha and everyone in the 100,000km radius.
That weapon would have brought great calamity had Kent not seized it when he did. She would have severely wounded Avotha, and if motivated enough, she would have succeeded in killing him, too.
The spear has a deadly track record, the kind that Kent doesn’t know, but he felt deep within his soul that it must be seized before it was successfully activated.
As if arranged by fate, Kent’s presence was vital in that critical moment.
But he himself, for a moment there, found himself in danger. By seizing the spear, he had unknowingly destroyed the plan crafted by the Demon King of the Graves Demon Continent.

He had been waiting patiently for Avotha to kill Warlord Biana so he could take the spear he had eyed for thousands of years. Now, he had lost that, and on top of that, he was afraid of the beautiful lady by Kent’s side.
While it was admirable how Kent cleaved through his attack, he wasn’t afraid of him. Killing Kent would be very simple. However, Inaya’s presence was a danger to him, so he retreated.

In the future, when he is capable, he will seek out Kent, and regardless of who is beside him, he will get the spear that, should he have gotten his hands on it, would propel him to the rank of a god much more easily.
Inaya smirked, watching the demon king retreat.
"You really should learn who you pick fights with."
Kent chuckled and took her hand, placing it on his chest. "I knew you wouldn’t let him bully me."
Inaya shook her head, clearly understanding how shameless her man is. But knowing he could rely on her made her feel special.
’Good thing you retreated, bastard. How I would have enjoyed cutting you down.’

Kent could feel the unmistakable Evil Qi that had always oozed from Inaya’s body whenever she planned something evil. This made him thank the stars for the demon king, who may have just made the best decision of his life.
Turning slightly, she regarded the battle between Vargus and the two demigods. One had lost an arm, and the other was barely holding her scythe.
The brute held an amused expression on his face:

"It is amusing, really. I had in the past fought harrowing demons and slaughtered them in a few swings." He blocked the stabbing attack from the one-armed demigod and pushed back. Then he ducked before his foot rose and landed a backward kick on the female demigod.
"It is a bit shocking you two still manage to hold on for this long," he said, and he jumped into the air, raising his axe overhead, both hands gripping the wooden handle.
Three runes ignited on his veined arm, sending torrents of energy into the axe. "You two are decent warriors. Too bad I have to kill you now."
Just when he was about to descend with his attack, Kent appeared before the two demigods and pressed his finger against their foreheads.
"Look into my eye,"

With their eyes widened from the danger descending on them, they stared deep into his eyes. A moment later, their arms went limp, and they dropped to their knees. Then life slowly slipped out of their bodies.
Kent became pale, dropping to his knees. Almost all soul energy was drained from his body. Inside the Soul Universe, thousands of soul spirits exploded, flooding his soul with soul essence.
COUGH COUGH
"Are you alright?" Inaya’s panicked voice entered his ears.
"I am fine, love. I just wanted to see how far I can stretch my soul," he paused, and inside his soul sea, his soul’s body looked up at the crack that had formed in the air...
"I guess I overestimated myself."
Inaya frowned, "Of course you did, you dumb bastard. Do you really think the soul of a mortal is strong enough to kill two demigods?"
Kent looked at the bodies of the two dead demigods, "I mean—"
"Shut up and let me heal you," she pressed her palm against his back, and a torrent of soul energy surged into his soul sea, causing the blood sea to surge.𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
"How are you not dead right now?" Inaya asked...
"You will understand soon,"

A few seconds later, her brow raised. "I see. Looks like you aren’t that weak in soul arts. But I am still pissed, and I am pretty sure my sisters will be pretty pissed when they learn of what you have done."
"Your sisters, huh. I like the sound of that,"
"Shut up,"
All around, everyone turned and looked at them, some wondering just what Kent had done, while others tried to make sense of what any of this meant.

They couldn’t understand why this battle started. All they knew was that Warlord Biana was one of the most dangerous people on Planet Skar. Many fear her; even the demon king is wary of her. So for her to be attacked at her base of operations, they couldn’t wrap their minds around it.
Most shocking, however, was that a 6th person was locked in battle with someone whom many didn’t know.
However, if they had a faint idea who that tattooed-faced man was, by now, all of them would be rallying with Uncle Drake to kill him. Granted, he was already in terrible shape.

Even Kent didn’t know why this battle was happening in the first place. He was spending a great time with his wife when he sensed a sudden invocation of his name, only to emerge at the center of a battle his legion was waging.
He didn’t even know how it happened, but he had stopped a massacre from a cursed weapon and even killed two demigods—barely clinging on to his life afterward.
In fact, feeling his soul slowly mend, he had one other person to thank.
Seated at the edge of the Mountain Garden, the bald kid shook his head and muttered, "Big brother is as reckless as ever,"
Kent’s voice then entered his head, causing him to frown, "Thanks, Baldy."
"I don’t like that name, Big Brother."
"Too bad. Until you grow a strand of hair, your name will always be Baldy, so get used to it,"
He pouted and shot his legs a few times before jumping off the edge, plummeting toward the crystal ground of Gaiaville.
He never went splat. Instead, he landed with a gentle grace and walked toward a candy store, muttering curses under his breath, "Bastard Big Brother,"
Back on the battlefield, Kent smirked and turned to Vargus... "What are you guys doing here?"
Before he could answer, the void cracked, and Axiom walked out holding a cube-shaped artifact forged from what appeared to be void stone.
He turned and waved at Kent, "Master, you are here too,"

"Yes, I am here, Axiom." He grinned and turned his gaze to the cube, causing Axiom to hide it behind him. But it was already too late, "Why don’t you hand over the Void Prison for safekeeping, buddy?"
