All they knew was that Warlord Biana was one of the most dangerous people on Planet Skar.
Many fear her; even the demon king is wary of her.
So for her to be attacked at her base of operations, they couldn’t wrap their minds around it.
Most shocking, however, was that a 6th person was locked in battle with someone whom many didn’t know.
However, if they had a faint idea who that tattooed-faced man was, by now, all of them would be rallying with Uncle Drake to kill him.
Granted, he was already in terrible shape.
Even Kent didn’t know why this battle was happening in the first place.
He was spending a great time with his wife when he sensed a sudden invocation of his name, only to emerge at the center of a battle his legion was waging.
He didn’t even know how it happened, but he had stopped a massacre from a cursed weapon and even killed two demigods—barely clinging on to his life afterward.
In fact, feeling his soul slowly mend, he had one other person to thank.
Seated at the edge of the Mountain Garden, the bald kid shook his head and muttered, "Big brother is as reckless as ever,"
Kent’s voice then entered his head, causing him to frown, "Thanks, Baldy."
"I don’t like that name, Big Brother."
"Too bad.
Until you grow a strand of hair, your name will always be Baldy, so get used to it,"
He pouted and shot his legs a few times before jumping off the edge, plummeting toward the crystal ground of Gaiaville.
He never went splat.
Instead, he landed with a gentle grace and walked toward a candy store, muttering curses under his breath, "Bastard Big Brother,"
Back on the battlefield, Kent smirked and turned to Vargus...
"What are you guys doing here?"
Before he could answer, the void cracked, and Axiom walked out holding a cube-shaped artifact forged from what appeared to be void stone.
He turned and waved at Kent, "Master, you are here too,"
"Yes, I am here, Axiom." He grinned and turned his gaze to the cube, causing Axiom to hide it behind him.
But it was already too late, "Why don’t you hand over the Void Prison for safekeeping, buddy?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1532: The Rescue
paragraphs: Axiom tried to protest, but in the end, he reluctantly handed over the Void Prison to Kent.
"No need to cry, Axiom. I will only take a few of them, provided they meet the requirements I have in mind," Kent wasn’t planning on depriving his subordinates of fine delicacies.
Axiom and his fellow Void Beasts feed on blood essence, the main blood and soul of their victims. It was one of the monstrous innate abilities of Void Beasts that made them terrifying beings.

Killing one person or beast gives them three sources of essence to absorb. Those who even devour the body gain four. So, based on the number of immortals Axiom had absorbed, there is a big chance he would be reaching the Immortal Lord stage after devouring them.
If Kent were to deprive him of that, it would be the most evil thing he would ever do to any of his subordinates.
Thankfully, Kent only wanted those who had the mark of Soul Warrior candidates. For reasons he can’t yet explain, he can now see those who, after their death, will become Soul Warrior candidates.
Maybe it was because his soul had become more robust after recalling all memories of Jest.
The demigods he killed had the mark. That was why he stole Vargus’ kills. Now, however, he wants to see if he can find more of them inside the Void Prison.
After that was settled, Vargus proceeded to tell him the details of their mission.
"So all this destruction was merely to save some princess,"
"Yes," Vargus nodded. "It was a side mission we received after clearing the 11th floor of the dungeon."
"I see." Kent turned and looked at Avotha, who held Warlord Biana by the neck.
"Vargus, you said the mission said killing the warlord is optional, right?"
The brute Shadow Rider nodded.
"In that case," Kent called out to Avotha, "Buddy, place a death seal on her instead. Such a fine warrior shouldn’t be wasted through senseless death,"
Avotha nodded and stretched his left hand, pressing his thumb against her forehead. On his chest, a tattoo of a triangular eye glowed, then moved along his arm and merged with her forehead.
Avotha then formed a hand seal, causing his third eye to release waves of death Qi. The energy flowed into the triangular eye tattoo, causing Warlord Biana to spasm before losing consciousness.
The moment the other immortals saw that their leader had been defeated, they scrambled and ran. Soon, every last one of them vanished, running as fast as their legs could carry them.
Up in the air, the two Immortal Lords that Fero took on came crashing to the ground. Fero let out a powerful roar and took a nosedive, stabbing his claws into their chests.

After wriggling for a few moments, they couldn’t hold on for long and passed out. It would take more than a stab to the chest to kill an Immortal Lord, especially if the attack came from an Immortal King.
But Fero never planned to kill them in the first place.

To him, expanding his master’s Undead Dragon Legion is of importance. So he will kidnap them, and after treating their injuries, they will be sent into the Dragon Ascension Realm to take the trial just like he did.
After checking if they had really passed out, he tossed them directly into the tower prison. The tower will handle their injuries.
He then transformed into his demi-dragon form, revealing a large wound on his chest. He gave it a brief look and turned away, his gaze landing on Kent.
They had met once, but it was brief. This time, however, they would have the chance to talk.
But before that, Kent turned and looked at Axiom. "Fetch the prisoner you are here for,"
He nodded and vanished back into the void. In the next few seconds, he appeared somewhere in the Silent Graves camp. He landed a kick on the door and walked in.
Just when he was about to take a turn, a dagger flew past his face, barely missing his nose.

"Wow, wow, slow down there, Rabbit. I am here to save Luciana." He raised his hand in surrender and stepped out, turning to his left. There, he saw five ladies dressed in maid clothing, with slave collars around their necks.

Three of them were demonkin, judging by the horns on their foreheads. The one who threw the dagger had dark horns, while the other two had green and red horns. The fourth was an elf whose green hair and eyes suggested she was a Green Elf. The last, however, was a Rabbitkin.

"Gotcha. You must be Luciana. My name is Axiom, right hand of the legendary Primordial Chaos Dragon. An undisputed void architect whose void traps have claimed the lives of powerful supremes and Celestials. The undisputed warrior who claimed the life of the crown prince of House Draham."
Axiom paused when he noticed the five ladies were giving him a creepy look. "What, do I have something on my face?"
They didn’t reply to him. Seeing that, he smirked and chose not to continue his introduction. In his mind, their mundane minds lacked the capacity to comprehend the sheer weight of his achievements.
"Anyways, my friends and I were sent here to rescue you, so let’s get moving."
He turned to leave, but Luciana didn’t move to follow him. He stopped and looked at her. "Why aren’t you coming?"
"How do I know you are who you say you are?"

Axiom frowned deeply. "I don’t have time to explain myself to any of you. All I can say is, I was sent here to fetch you. So come with me willingly, or I will drag you like a sac full of dead bodies."
Luciana frowned, and the demonkin who threw the dagger moved to shield her. Seeing this, Axiom smirked and was about to pull Luciana into the void when Kailan appeared.
"Come on, Axiom. Must everything be solved with violence?"
"If not violence, then what else?" He smirked and regarded the princess again before stepping back for Kailan. He knew Kent sent Kailan, knowing the kind of unhinged bastard he really is.
’Master sure knows me.’ Being recognized as an unhinged bastard made him feel proud of himself.

Seeing the smile on his face, Kailan shook his head and retrieved a contract from his space ring, showing its seal to the five ladies. The moment Luciana saw the seal, she rushed forward to have a closer look.
"This...!"
"It is the seal of the high priestess of the Green-Skin Rabbitkin race. My name is Kailan, a member of Kent Madson’s legion. He sent us to come get you,"
"Kent Madson," the red-horned demon jumped forward and asked before Luciana could.
"Indeed. That Kent Madson. He is a few blocks away. Your master has been captured, so you are free to go. If you want to meet him too, feel free to follow us,"
Kailan turned and looked at Princess Luciana. "Are you ready to leave now?"
She nodded and then turned to the four other maids behind her. "But they are coming with us too."
"The more, the merrier." Soon, Kailan led the five ladies out and headed toward Kent’s direction. After they were gone, Axiom smirked.
"What a headache. I could have just kidnapped them and made everything short," he smirked a second time and then headed deeper into the mansion.

Since the owner of this camp was dead, naturally, her treasure vault needed a new owner. Axiom, who is known for stealing from even Celestials, knew he had to do justice to the treasures hidden within.

chapters.title: Chapter 1533: Five Maids
paragraphs: With Kailan taking the lead, they soon arrived at the battleground.
So far, the battle against the Silent Graves was over. The only one still raging was the one between Uncle Drake and the Tattooed Man.
"Master, this is Princess Luciana, the one we were sent to rescue, and her friends."
Kent turned and looked at the Rabbitkin, then at the four other maids with her. His gaze turned to the slave collar around their neck, causing him to frown.
"Kenna," Kent called out, and the sexy soul warrior appeared and leaned on his shoulder. When Inaya saw this, she frowned. However, her expression softened the next moment.
"Take care of their slave collars."
"Okay, Master." Kenna moved toward the five ladies and extended her hand, causing five identical runes to fly out and merge with the shackles around their necks.
The next second, a clicking sound was heard, and the slave collars that could only be removed by the slave master came undone, clattering to the ground.

Everyone who witnessed this gasped, some even wondering just what the hell had just happened. A slave master has complete control over the slave collars that they put around the necks of their slaves. Before that connection can be broken, the slave master must willingly cut it, or it automatically breaks when they are dead.
Warlord Biana is not dead yet, so her hold over the five maids remains intact.
That, of course, means they cannot be freed. However, in what could be said to be a simple wave of the hand, all five collars came off.
"Why does it feel like all I have learned and known in the 100,000 years I have lived seems to be useless when trying to understand these people?"
"Where are they from? Who are they, and why does it feel like the most monstrous of them is that dragon kid with the beautiful hair?"
"Indeed. They all seem to refer to him as master, yet I don’t see any slave collar or slave mark on them."
"Very strange indeed. I wonder which powerhouse gave birth to such a monster."

While everyone was filled with questions with no answers, Inaya looked at Kenna and then turned to Kent and asked, "How was she able to do that? Even it would have taken me a minute to sever the slave link."
Kent smiled and looked at Kenna before answering, "She is special."
Kenna liked her master’s response, so she kissed him on the cheek before vanishing back into the Soul Universe. Inaya smirked but planned to ask Vexthra and the rest of her sisters.

If only she knew that not even Vexthra had met the three soul warriors Kent had created so far. Kenna was the second soul warrior, whose nature as a Void Reaper enabled her to infiltrate souls unnoticed and sever soul connections.

Her [Astral Severance] allows her to perceive the connections linked to the soul and sever them. She usually has to enter the soul, which she could do using the void. So the slave collars were merely trinkets before her.
After she was gone, Kent turned and looked at the five ladies, who had become stunned, staring at the shackles that had bound their souls in servitude for years now broken on the ground.
"I know you all have questions, which I will answer. But for now, follow Kailan. He will take you somewhere to rest. I will come see you when I am done here."
They nodded, and before long, they appeared somewhere in Gaiaville.
Kent and the rest continued to wait for Uncle Drake to finish torturing the poor Tattooed Man. Thankfully, after a few minutes, he managed to bring him to the door of death.
[Master, I would like to harvest this man’s soul,] from within the Soul Universe, Bello, Kent’s third soul warrior, requested.
Kent didn’t even have to ask what he would do with it since he knew Bello was basically the Grim Reaper, or at least a messenger of the Grim Reaper.
Hearing his request, he called out to his old-time friend, "Uncle Drake, a subordinate of mine needs his soul, so if you don’t mind."
Turning sharply, Uncle Drake’s eyes finally landed on Kent, bringing a smile to his face. He took one step and appeared before Kent, the Tattooed Man, held by the neck.
"Long time no see, Kid, or should I say Chaos?"
"Whichever you prefer, old friend." Uncle Drake laughed joyfully and tossed the near-death Tattooed Man to Avotha, who caught him and pressed his finger against his forehead.
This time, instead of sealing him, he mouthed a few creepy words and pulled back his finger, reaping out an astral copy of the Tattooed Man, his soul.
The man screamed and tried to fight back, but it was futile. All around watching, many flinched, and a few took several steps back, their backs breaking into cold sweat.
Avotha retrieved a black talisman and pressed it against the forehead of the soul he had extracted. It shrank, and before long, the only thing that remained was a ball of soul.
Kent reached for it, and after a quick look, it vanished into the Soul Universe, appearing before Bello.
[Thank you, Master. I will be going into seclusion now. Once I am out, I will hopefully reach the Immortal Emperor or Immortal Monarch stage.]
’Good luck, buddy. Just don’t be there for too long. It won’t be long before we embark on our final mission in the High World.’
[Okay, Master.]
Uncle Drake sized Avotha up and smiled. "Some friends you have, Chaos."

Kent smirked and turned toward the darkness a couple of kilometers away. "The same can be said for you. If I didn’t know better, I would say she is one of those creepy shadows that used to follow you around."

Uncle Drake smiled and scratched his head. "My Dragon Warriors all fell during the Great War, but fate had mercy on their souls and reincarnated them. I have only managed to reunite with Daliah and Umai."
"Daliah was the one who severed my ear back then, right?"
Uncle Drake laughed and tapped Kent on the shoulder. "You aren’t still hung up on that humiliation, are you?"
"Of course not. I have already formed millions of ways to torture her. But that is all in the past now. I am a new person, a changed person, if you will."
Kent turned and looked at the darkness and smiled. "Daliah dear, no need to hide from me. Big Daddy Chaos has already forgiven you."
Hidden inside the darkness, Daliah trembled, her legs turning wobbly. Kent could not see her, but Inaya, Avotha, and Uncle Drake could.
Seeing her reaction, Inaya grabbed Kent’s slightly long dragon ear and pulled on it. "Stop scaring the young lady."
Inaya turned and looked at Daliah. "Hi, my name is Inaya, the Ten Emotions Sword Supreme. Why don’t you come out? I will not allow this brat to hurt you."
Daliah hesitated for a few seconds, and then she cleared the darkness. It was then that everyone saw why she had put up the darkness in the first place.
They all gasped, some taking even more steps back.

All around the black mansion, three Demigods and twenty-four Immortal Lords had been tied up using a strange-looking red rope, all of them unconscious. The rest had been killed, their heads arranged into a pyramid.

chapters.title: Chapter 1534: Old Enemy
paragraphs: Before meeting the Flame King, Chaos had already heard a lot of stories about him. They claimed he was someone on the same level as him.

They claimed he had single-handedly held back a beast tide that had ten Demigod-level beasts when he was merely an Immortal Lord. They said many things about him, each one sounding more unbelievable than the other.
Eventually, the stories started to include some other people, whom Chaos later came to know as the 24 Dragon Guards.

Before meeting the 69 Void Beasts and recruiting them to become his guides while inside the void realm, who later became his team, Chaos actually saw the 24 Dragon Guards as the most disciplined and terrifying team he had ever met.

The day he and the Flame King met, they fought a great battle. In the end, Chaos defeated him, barely, but he was soon ambushed by the 24 Dragon Guards. He knew he couldn’t defeat them, so he made a run for it.
He escaped and when he was out of danger, he let out a breath and was about to slow down and make his next move when his shadow moved, and before he could react, his ear came off.

It was that day he met Daliah, one of the most dangerous assassins to ever live during the Primordial Era. She cut his ear off, and that humiliation drove Chaos to seek revenge, ultimately resulting in a great battle between him and the Flame King.
He never got that revenge since teh flame King never gave him the chance.
Today, the woman who made him feel the most humiliated during the primordial era appeared before him again, bringing with her all the past pain he had suppressed.
Their eyes met, and for a brief moment, the pain he experienced when his ear came off flowed into his mind. This caused him to sigh and then smirk.
"Nice meeting you again, Daliah."
She stood there for a few seconds, then bowed. "Greetings to you too, Lord Chaos."
Inaya walked to Daliah’s side and pulled her into her arms. Seeing this, Kent chuckled and turned to Uncle Drake. "Let’s take this to the tower."
He nodded, and before long, everyone vanished, including the dead bodies of every last person they had killed. The tied-up demigods and immortal lords were also taken away.
The people who witnessed the battle were all left wondering so many things.
Eventually, they dispersed as well, and the news began to spread widely.

The name Chaos soon started to spread, causing many to wonder if there was a second Kent Madson on the rise. The sheer details in the spread, along with the exaggeration, painted Chaos as some kind of prodigy who appears once every era.
Eventually, word reached an immortal world called Solan. It is the home planet of the Supreme White Tiger Clan.
Many years ago, when Kent was in the Pill World, he accepted a quest to kill a Planet King. Back then, he didn’t know who this Planet King was.
Later, however, he found out he was someone who had absorbed the blood essence of the Forsaken Race, hoping to use unnatural ways to break through the limit of the High World.

Kent succeeded in killing him. However, what he didn’t know was that the Planet King he killed was actually a young prince of the Supreme White Tiger Clan named Kaine. By killing him, he became the enemy of the entire clan.
They knew the one who killed their prince was someone named Chaos. They had placed a bounty on him, and for years now, they had been searching for him.
When word reached them that a kid named Chaos had appeared on a planet not that far from their star system, they deployed five Demigods to bring him in.
Unfortunately for them, Kent was long gone by the time they arrived.
It pained their hearts. However, after making inquiries for a while, they managed to get a drawing of Kent. Along the way, after asking many questions, they also found something very interesting.

It turned out that when Inaya introduced herself to Daliah, she accidentally revealed her true identity. Hearing that she had been with Chaos the whole time, they immediately returned to their home world to report.
"The Ten Emotions Sword Supreme, huh," a man with an overflowing aura—one that not even a Demigod would possess despite him only being at the Demigod stage—muttered, his expression calm.
His mind spun as he tried to recall something buried deep in his memory. After all, he had lived for over a million years, so there was just no telling how much knowledge he had accumulated.

His name is Cyrus, the current patriarch of the Supreme White Tiger Clan in the Immortal World. He became a god 200,000 years ago, but had decided to remain in the Immortal Realm for now while he handled the issue with his son’s murderer.
"Aaha... I remember now. The Ten Emotions Sword Supreme was a legendary swordswoman during the Divine Era. According to the records, she was the Dao Companion of the legendary Lord Genesis.
After the Divine War, nobody knew where she had vanished to. Some say she fell, others say she abandoned this universe and ascended to a much higher plane.
Later, however, it was discovered that she descended to a High World called Brymrr, which was the homeworld of Lord Genesis. She became their ruler, and for years, she had been there.
If she indeed was seen with that bastard, then maybe they are related."
"Then should we send people to Planet Brymrr and see if they can capture or kill that bastard?"

Lord Cyrus looked at his elder with disdain. "Do you even hear yourself? You want us to send our best to Planet Brymrr and hope we get a chance to kill someone who may be under the protection of that monster.

Do you even know how you sound right now? While many only heard stories about Lord Genesis, do not forget that he had a partner who was equally lethal. She was someone who walked side by side with a legend.

Do you seriously think such a person is someone we want to mess with? Even if we send a Supreme to that place, the chances of them returning in one piece are low. We can’t afford to antagonize someone like that right now.
For now, let’s keep an eye on that planet and report whatever you observe. If we manage to get a chance one day, we will take it.
For now, we can only observe and hope the ancestors in the Supreme and Celestial Worlds will have pity on us and send someone to come and aid us."
The elders nodded, all of them sighing in a defeated manner. They had searched for a long time, only to retreat when they finally managed to locate the brat they were looking for.
After the elders left the hall, Lord Cyrus sighed again. "Damnit. Just when I got close, this bastard had to have someone this powerful backing him."

He let out a third sigh, stood up, and walked away. When he was gone, a moth on the wall grew wings and flew away. After a while, it landed in a vast desert and transformed into a young man with butterfly wings and antennae.
He is a Demigod with a wisp of divine qi in his blood.
"I need to report to my Lady." He again took flight and vanished into the clouds.

chapters.title: Chapter 1535: Uncle Drake’s Revenge
paragraphs: Uncle Drake’s return to the tower again brought waves of joy to everyone.
Kent’s wives, who had known and interacted with him back in the Sonox, were happy to see him again, and so were some of the legion.
Not all of them are familiar with him, but the majority of them are, and so his presence brought them waves of happiness.

Uncle Drake had briefly lived and fought beside them during the clash with the Ancient Sea Race and the Ancient Vampires. It was a dreadful battle that claimed the lives of many but also brought everyone together.
Shortly after the battle, however, Uncle Drake vanished.

Seeing him back, and as an Immortal Monarch no less, made them all happy. Kent was also happy to see the Drake he had helped become a dragon back when he and the selected few from the Half-Elf race ventured into the Flame Valley, now back by his side.
They spent some time inside the Legion Tower catching up with everyone. Soon, however, the two of them moved to the Mountain Garden to have a proper talk.
Kent had some things—in fact, he had quite a lot of things to do—so he had no plans to waste any time.
Appearing in the Mountain Garden, Uncle Drake regarded the four cities in the distance and smiled.
"I like what you have done with the place, Chaos. The last time I was here, there was only a small mansion standing somewhere over there."

Kent nodded. "Indeed, I have come a long way. But the same can be said of you. You are now an Immortal Monarch, though I can’t say I am surprised, considering I suspect you have all your memories back."

Kent walked to a swinging chair and sat down, letting his leg drift in the air a few times. "Dare I ask what happened, Uncle Drake? The last time we talked, you said you were taking a short trip. That was three years ago.
Now, you have become an Immortal monarch and seem to be on a path of revenge, something I know you do only if the offense is grave and cannot be forgiven. What happened?"
Drawing on his memories of when he and Uncle Drake were pals, he knew that if his old friend were to return to his former cold, ruthless self, this universe would soon go up in flames.
"A lot had indeed happened, Chaos. I did take a short trip; however, that trip turned out to be the beginning of a journey that thrust me back into the dreadful life I had once lived."
Uncle Drake also sat down and started to reveal what happened.

"I had planned to stay in Sonox for the 1,000 years I promised. However, that changed when I battled with Leviathan. During our battle, he attacked me with a mental attack. Of course, I survived; however, that was when everything changed.
Although I survived that mental attack, after the battle, I started to see these flashes in my mind.

Most of these flashes contained the name of a planet. At first, I pushed them aside and decided to spend the next 1,000 years in Sonox as I had planned. However, I soon realized doing so would be torture.
It was then that I decided to find out what was wrong with my memories.
So, after healing Leviathan, I made him the new guardian and left for the planet I kept seeing in my memories. It took me a few months, but I eventually found it.
That was when everything changed.
The moment I stepped on that planet, I felt all these memories rushing back to me. In those memories, I saw a life I had once lived, a life filled with so many experiences.
It took a while to make sense of it. But when I did, I saw the whole picture. I was the Flame King, the one who commanded one of the Sacred Flames—the Flames of Immortality.
After I recovered my memories, I knew I had to seek out my subordinates, who had been promised by you that they would reincarnate one day in the future."

"I did, didn’t I?" Kent smiled, his mind going back to the moment the 12 Universe Guardians abandoned the Universe and used the gift bestowed on them by the Heart of the Universe to ascend to the ????? universe.
He saw no end to the chaos, and so he turned to his friend, Ignarax, and asked him something nobody in their right mind would accept.
Ignarax, however, did—he accepted to ignite the Flame of Immortality and burned away the karma of all tainted souls, finally unleashing the immolating Flames of Immortality.
His request, however, was for his 24 Dragon Guards to have a good life in their next life. Chaos accepted his request and made him an even better promise.
He promised to reincarnate their souls alongside his somewhere in the future.

"I guess you did. I soon found Daliah, who had been looking for me too. It turns out that when they died, one of her shadows, still holding a flicker of her soul, remained hidden in my shoulder, allowing her to hear our last conversation, and so when she was reborn, she started to look for me.
When we reunited, she took me to Umai."
"Umai, she was the Crystal Dragon, if I remember correctly."
"Indeed. She had also reincarnated and had made a life for herself. She founded a Dragon Enclave and had been going all over the universe rescuing stray dragons and looking after them."
Kent smiled. "She was always the caring one. Sometimes I wonder why she chose to follow you."

Uncle Drake smiled and said in a guilty tone, "I happen to be the killer of her two brothers and father. You can say she was my slave for a few hundred thousand years, but we later reconciled, and she became my greatest soldier."
"You were indeed a scum of society back then. No wonder I tried killing you many times."
They regarded each other, then burst into resounding laughter.

The Flame King was indeed a plague for the better half of his life during the Primordial Era. However, that is all in the past now. He had paid his dues with his life, buying Chaos ample time to unleash the Spell of Origin.

"When I met her, she happened to have found one of my Flame Hearts and prepared treasures for me to ascend to the rank of an Immortal so I could absorb it. Since my foundation is still strong—even stronger than before—I swiftly leveled up.
After a year and a half, I reached the Core Immortal stage, so I decided to absorb the Flame Heart.

Nothing, however, prepared me for what happened when I entered seclusion. It turned out that a dragon prince from a rather powerful dragon family learned of the Flame Heart in my possession and mobilized three other Demigods to help him claim it.
Their attack was sudden and devastating. In the end, they failed and were repelled by Daliah and Umai. However, three kids under Umai’s care died in the clash, and Umai was gravely injured.
After I was done absorbing the Flame Heart, I made provision for her and the kids and embarked on a revenge mission to kill those four scums.
The first one was the tattooed guy I killed on Planet Skar. It took some time to track him down, but I did, and thanks to your power, I was able to slay him.
I still have three more to kill. For now, I will bide my time and locate them. Daliah had already sent her shadows to track them down."

Kent sighed. "Sorry to hear about Umai and her kids. Of course, while I can’t actively aid you in the search for the three Demigods, I can help with Umai and her kids. If you want, they can move in here and stay with my people."

chapters.title: Chapter 1536: Promise of a Dragon
paragraphs: "You know, Chaos, back when you created the Spell of Origin, every last one of us laughed at you. Sure, you were the strongest among us, the legendary Primordial Chaos Dragon.
In fact, you were also the only being to touch the laws of Origin. However, that was the Primordial Era, not the Unknown Era.
The laws were static, hard to bend or even fully comprehend. So claiming you had created a spell that transcends all laws was just ridiculous.
However, now that I sit before you, alive, with my memories intact, I have to say, I shouldn’t have doubted you. None of us, especially the dragon council, should have doubted you.
For that, I am sorry. You have done more than enough for me, so I can’t in good conscience ask you for more."
Kent smirked and waved his hand, taking out two gourds of wine. He threw one toward Uncle Drake and gulped down a mouthful from his gourd.

"There is no need to be emotional, Uncle Drake. We fought on the same battlefield and bled for this universe. Naturally, that makes us brothers, so if I have the means to protect the people under your care, I naturally wouldn’t hesitate.
Of course, knowing one of the people who attacked you is from a powerful dragon family is all the reason you need to move your people here.

When we go for revenge and manage to kill that scum, they will retaliate, and so we wouldn’t want them coming back to where it all began to finish the job. There are kids involved here, so their safety is of great importance."
"Thank you, Chaos," Uncle Drake said before taking a gulp of his drink, too.
The tower city is now expanding. The four cities are now occupied by millions of people. Naturally, they are all adding to Kent’s soul strength.

He may only be at the Tier 19 stage for now; however, thanks to the worlds he has linked to his soul and the people living in the tower, his true soul strength is comparable to that of someone at the Tier 25 stage.

That would only continue to strengthen once he reaches the Immortal stage. So adding more people works in his favor. He has billions of tower points, so no one living in the tower would lack anything.
There is nothing like poverty inside the tower.
"I have some things to handle later. Once done, we will head over to where Umai and the kids are so we can bring them back to the tower."
Uncle Drake nodded. He drank yet another gulp and exhaled.
"It feels good to be back, Chaos. I know many eras have passed, but now that I am back, I feel like I will be living the best lifetime around," he laughed, clenching his fist lightly.
"The last time, we lost to the Void Beasts; this time around, we won’t."

Kent smiled and gulped down yet another mouthful. He usually doesn’t drink; however, when an old friend from the distant past finally returns to his side, drinking a few gourds is nothing.𝙛𝒓𝒆𝙚𝒘𝒆𝓫𝙣𝓸𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝒄𝒐𝓶

"We indeed lost severely, my brother, but this time, we have to be more prepared than the last. I have only recently started to recall my memories, but I have already seen that in the eras that followed, similar battles occurred, and, as before, only a few were won.

This means those threats still remain. One day, they will find their way to us, and I am afraid we are not prepared yet. So we must grab every opportunity we can get our hands on because, believe it or not, this time, we will feel true despair, and I myself cannot wait to experience it," Kent laughed, causing Uncle Drake to shake his head.
"You know, Chaos, the last time, when the dragon council learned you had ventured into the Void Realm, we debated whether or not you were indeed sound in the head.
Don’t get me wrong, some of us became afraid when the first battle was over. Most of our brothers and sisters were severely injured, some dying from that battle.

However, a year later, you ventured there as if your life were useless. I even argued that maybe you wanted to die and so you offered your neck to them," Uncle Drake smirked and shook his head in defeat.
"The only one who saw some semblance of normalcy in you was the Rainbow Dragon Monarch. Of course, she was smitten with you, so you can say she wanted to paint a good picture of you.
We all said you had gone mad, and I guess we were right. Hearing you now, I can say for a fact you have gone mad, Chaos. Does any of what you just said sound like a reason to make you happy?
Do you even value your life?"
Kent laughed, throwing his head back.
All over Gaiaville and beyond, many turned and looked toward the mountain garden. Even his wives, who were taking a tour through the tower cities, looked in the direction of the mountain garden.
They had never heard Kent laugh that heartily before.
Seated under a pavilion, Baldy looked toward the mountain garden and smirked. "Crazy Big Brother."
"Ignarax, buddy, my life is one thing I cherish more than anything. I have over two dozen wives who need me, so if I don’t value my life, it would mean I don’t value them.

However, I am also the Primordial Chaos Dragon. In my veins run streams of blood that originated from the Primal Chaos. I thrive in chaos. Chaotic moments made me strong, so if there are universe-ending battles coming, naturally, I ought to be happy."

He stood up and walked to the edge of the mountain garden. "You know, for a very long time, I roamed the universe uncontested. Everywhere I went, nobody matched my prowess. The likes of the Great Axe Monarch, Supreme Whip Empress, and many more challenged me, but all fell short.
I was so bored that I sometimes ventured into the Primal Zones just to have a taste of danger. It was also then that I first met the void beast.
The first Void Beast I fought was a True God, and I was merely a Demigod. That day, I saw despair for the first time, and you know what—"
Kent turned and looked at Uncle Drake. "It was beautiful."

"There I was, my defense completely dismantled, my life hanging on by a thread, and pain rocking my very soul. However, instead of fear, I felt alive. For the first time in millions of years, I felt like living indeed has some purpose.

Since then, I realized something else. I realized my power comes from chaos, so whenever there is chaos, I ought to be there. This is why I was able to defeat the likes of you despite being surrounded by many subordinates.

The more furious the battle rages on, the stronger I get until I am the most dangerous thing on the battlefield. So yes, I am a little bit crazy and perhaps a bit mad, but I believe I am just what this universe needs, don’t you think?"
Uncle Drake drank his last gulp and also walked toward the edge of the mountain garden, letting the cold breeze brush against his face.

"I guess you indeed are what we need. But this time, you won’t be the only one thriving in the chaos. This time, the Flame King, whose flame burns even Immortality, will be by your side, raining down fire on their heads."
The two dragons threw their heads back and let out thunderous laughter, their shoulders shaking.

Sure, you were the strongest among us, the legendary Primordial Chaos Dragon.
In fact, you were also the only being to touch the laws of Origin.
However, that was the Primordial Era, not the Unknown Era.
The laws were static, hard to bend or even fully comprehend.
So claiming you had created a spell that transcends all laws was just ridiculous.
However, now that I sit before you, alive, with my memories intact, I have to say, I shouldn’t have doubted you.
None of us, especially the dragon council, should have doubted you.
For that, I am sorry.
You have done more than enough for me, so I can’t in good conscience ask you for more."
Kent smirked and waved his hand, taking out two gourds of wine.
He threw one toward Uncle Drake and gulped down a mouthful from his gourd.

Naturally, that makes us brothers, so if I have the means to protect the people under your care, I naturally wouldn’t hesitate.

chapters.title: Chapter 1537: A Princess Worry
paragraphs: A few hours ago, when Kent, Inaya, and the others returned to the tower, Ainna was quick to rush to her friend’s side to inquire about a few things.

Initially, she wanted to scream at her for abandoning her for over 100 days. However, that fury washed away when she unceremoniously ventured into the harem tower and ended up seeing what she had no business seeing.
Now, she just wanted to check up on her. Of course, after spending a few days with Selene, her personality has slightly changed.
"You, what took you so long?" Ainna feigned ignorance, pretending she had no idea what had happened. Inaya also had no idea she saw her and Kent, so she smiled and blushed a little.
"We had a lot to talk about, Ainna."
Ainna furrowed her brow. "Talk? So you have been talking for 100 days, huh?"
"Like I said, there was a lot to be said, and so we had to say it all."
"I see. I guess you indeed had a lot to say to each other. I myself have some things to say to that bastard. That said," Ainna narrowed her eyes and looked at her friend critically.
"There is something different about you."
"Oh, you noticed." Inaya smiled and brushed her hair to the side. "I am on the verge of breaking through to the Supreme stage. Any moment from now, I can have my tribulation."
"Wow, really? I am happy for you, Inaya. Finally, you will also become a Supreme."

Ainna beamed with joy, happy for her friend. She had tried many times to help her over the years, but had failed each time. So, hearing she had finally made the final step, she felt waves of happiness for her.
She turned and looked in Kent’s direction and asked, "I suppose I can forgive him a bit for coming through for you. But I will still pull on his ear for his past transgressions."
"It isn’t his fault, Ainna. Just like me, he also had his fair share of troubles, so maybe lighten up a bit for him. Also, I wouldn’t want you getting hurt."
"Getting hurt?" Ainna smirked. "As if that bug can even lay a finger on a strand of my hair."
"That isn’t—" Inaya paused and smiled. "You know what, good luck. Don’t come running when he gets his hands on you."𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎

Ainna may not have known what she meant, but since she saw what her friend and Kent had been doing the past 100 days, she knew Inaya’s warning had to do with her being held by the head and throat-fucked.
Thinking about it made her body tremble slightly.
She never expected things to progress that fast between Kent and Inaya. But now that it did and she was there to bear witness to how wild it was, she would never forget.
Of course, she wished she could forget, but it was already too late. If she had waited for Inaya to come out on her own, she would have been free from all this awkwardness.
"Let’s go. The ladies want to show us around the tower." Holding each other’s hands, they walked away and joined Vexthra and the others.
Meanwhile, Axiom and the others transferred the captured demigods and immortals to the tower prison.

The ones Daliah captured were also brought along and sent to the tower prisons. Since the majority of them were Immortal Lords, they would be housed there until those who could use them gained the strength to do so.
Aside from them, Kent would also need some, as long as they met his requirements.
As for the dead bodies, they were given to Veera and Elaine, who became thrilled to receive such monstrous treasures.

Veera is a necromancer, so she would be creating terrifying undead from this haul. Elaine can summon Death Agents using dead bodies. For now, she only took three Immortal Emperor bodies and entered her Life & Death space with her three Death Agents to cultivate.
The rest of the bodies were put in storage. Yi Lai had also entered seclusion to attempt to break past the Heavenly Ascension stage.

Having eight Immortal-level undead dragons under her command was as far as she could go while still at the Heavenly Ascension stage. If she were to break past that stage, then she could send at least one of the demigods into the Dragon Ascension Trial and finally welcome a demigod undead.
For now, she could only hope for the best.
But even if she can’t do much now, once Kent returns from Elina’s galaxy, they will be ascending to the Immortal World, where she can ascend without having to break any limits.
So, the ladies left the legion tower and headed to Gaiaville first. They started the tour from there. Soon, they made their way to Blood City.
The crimson city was a sight to behold. The five maids, who had lived almost their entire lives on Planet Skar, felt more at home there.
Where they came from was all crimson, regardless of the time of day, so being surrounded by crimson walls and pavements made them even more drawn to this place.
Later, they moved to Skyjade City, where the Sky Foxes live. They spent quite some time there, since it is one of the tower’s wonders.

A city floating with nothing holding it in place was something many hadn’t seen before. Of course, someone like Inaya and Ainna, who had lived for several eras already, had seen many wondrous sights, so a floating city wasn’t new to them.
Their admiration, however, came from its beauty. The city was built using jade, so it had a unique charm that, as they looked at it, warmed their hearts.
Its beauty was on another level.
Their tour then came to an end in Nature City, home of the Elves.
The moment they arrived there, Princess Luciana became a bit emotional. The ladies inquired why, and she said her world once looked naturally like Nature City.

However, after the battle with the Chaos Envoys, the planet’s dragon vein was damaged, so slowly, while still holding on, her world would eventually die, and over 15 million of her kin would perish with it. Unless, of course, they find a new planet to occupy.
It was a bit sad when they heard what she said.
Because of that, their tour was cut short because they decided to return to the 11th floor, which happens to be Planet Rainy.
That is Princess Luciana’s planet.
Vexthra wanted to meet the leaders of her race and have a talk with them.

While moving 15 million people into the tower wouldn’t be too much of a struggle, she wanted to make a trade with them. Luckily, Princess Luciana had seen what kind of paradise they would be coming to, and even better, she had finally been rescued.
The price they would have to pay would definitely be worth it.
With her divinity fully recovered, they soon made their way to the biggest city on the planet. That was where Axiom and his friends met the High Priestess and took the contract.
When they arrived with Princess Luciana, everyone became overjoyed. They all came to hug and welcome her back home, considering she had been away for several years.
Vexthra and her sisters were also welcomed with open arms. The mission was successful, and the princess had been rescued. Vexthra and her sisters joined in on the celebration.
Later, they met the High Priestess and some of the Elders to discuss the reason for their visit.

chapters.title: Chapter 1538: One of the Divine Zodiac Spears
paragraphs: Kent spent the entire day talking with Uncle Drake. He got to learn more about his old friend and comrade. When that came to an end, however, he retreated to the Sword Tower to handle a few things.
He was already aware that one of the Eternal Sword Intents left behind by Jest was now in the tower. He was happy to learn that.
In his memories, after glimpsing the realm beyond the Sword Celestial stage, he used what he had learned to refine seven strands of sword intent, putting everything he knew on the line.
In the end, he succeeded.
However, instead of the Celestial Sword Intent he expected, something else emerged. The sword intents were sentient. He was a bit stunned when all seven of them manifested into humanoid forms.
When this happened, Jest was stunned, but he soon learned that the path to the realm above the Sword Celestial stage would be achieved through the seven sword intents.
To do that, however, he sent them away with only one mission: to create a sword technique and master it to the point that it would transcend the realm of Sword Celestial.
After they left, he lost connection to all of them except Baldy.

Unless the other six, he manifested into a kid, and considering he was a bit clingy, he wanted to stay by Jest’s side. Unfortunately for him, Jest was a Sword Celestial back then, going into battle against a monster.
He was merely a child now growing.

So, using the excuse that he should wait for him on Planet Brymrr, Jest left, never to return. When Baldy learned he had died, he wept and chose to seal himself away, using the passage of time to learn and keep growing until they met again.
In past eras, he had protected Planet Brymrr from all threats. Now, he had returned to Kent’s side, still as a child but with overwhelming prowess.

Kent planned to spend some time with him, but before that, he wanted to have a clear idea of the spear he seized from Warlord Briana, the broken sword he bought at the auction, the Spirit Brush, and see where the path led next.
His wives informed him that they were taking Princess Luciana home, so he would be using the time he had to handle these issues.
Gaia had also informed him that they were done with 95% of the portal, so it wouldn’t be long before he was ready to head to Elina’s galaxy.
He brought out the spear and made it hover before him.
It seemed to have been made from a material that, to Kent, appeared like a stone and a bit like metal.
Given the texture, it would be a bit rough on the palm when wielded. It was exactly 2 meters long, and one end was razor-sharp and scaly.
Nine runes have been carved on its length.
"Good spear, though I see nothing special about it that would suggest why that demon king was eager to get it." Kent focused more on the runes on it but saw nothing special.
It was ordinary at best; however, he knew it was in no way a simple spear.
If anything, the feeling of dread he felt when Warlord Biana activated one of the runes on it told him the spear was a terrifying weapon and that he should be careful around it.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
"Tower, what do you have on this weapon?" Since he was making no progress, he turned to Tower, who seemed to know most things that he did not.
Unfortunately, no good answer came from the tower. However, she managed to give him something to go on.
[Regretfully, I have no idea what this spear is or where it came from. However, there is a way the Master can find out.]
"I am all ears, Tower."
[Although I have no idea what the spear is, I can tell it is a soul weapon, meaning it has a soul space. The Master can send a part of his consciousness inside and inspect it from within.
It isn’t linked to anyone, so there will be no defenses to break. If that yields no results, then we can save it for now and look for answers later.]
Kent saw no problem with that. He inhaled deeply and then exhaled. He formed a hand seal and sent a strange part of his soul toward the spear.
He held his breath, watching as the strand of soul essence drifted toward the spear. For a moment, he expected nothing to happen, but it did.
When it happened, he wasn’t prepared.

Just when his soul essence was close to the weapon, something took hold of it, and his entire soul was dragged into the spear, causing his body to fall backward and his soul to start falling into a dark hole.
Panic set in and was soon replaced by fear before he started to curse his life away. In a span of what felt like eternity, Kent cursed his bad luck several hundred times.
But then he didn’t go splat. Instead, he suddenly found himself standing in a large hall, its walls painted in ten different shades of color.
Kent took a deep breath and began examining his body. After a few minutes, he stopped and let out a relieved sigh. He was fine from head to toe, at least as far as his soul is concerned.
Once that was taken care of, he started to look around.

On the walls, he saw some writings, each with a background in a different color. He moved closer to the one with a green background. However, just when he was right before it, he found himself back to where he was.
"Hmmm, that is strange," Kent said, and then he moved again, stopping just where he had been before.
However, to his shock, it happened again.
"What in the hell is happening?" He tried three more times, but the same result.
So he switched to the blue wall and walked toward it. But then the same thing happened. He moved toward the red and three other colors, but the same thing happened.

Finally, Kent turned toward the golden color. He chose this because something clicked in his mind that he may have overlooked. When Warlord Biana used her life force to ignite the rune, it glowed golden.
Now, as he faced the golden wall, Kent hoped with every fiber of his being that he was right, or else he would go mad.
He took one step at a time, and before long, he was standing before the golden wall. He closed his eyes and exhaled, knowing the moment he opened them, he would be back at the center of the hall.
"Well then..."
He snapped them open, and his gaze landed on the golden wall. Instead of staring at it from ten meters away, he was looking at it from less than a meter away.
This caused him to blink a few times. The next moment, however, the wall began to change as several writings appeared on it.
He lifted his head and looked at the header, and it read...
"Here lies the monument of Vael’Zhor, the Zodiac Forgebinder, creator and forger of the Sunfang Tyrant Spear, one of the ten Divine Zodiac Spears."
Kent blinked once or twice, his mind spinning as he read the header of the writing. There were additional writings after the header; however, he couldn’t look past it.
He blinked again and read the header once more. Then he turned and began reading the texts that followed.

Unfortunately for him, Jest was a Sword Celestial back then, going into battle against a monster.
He was merely a child now growing.
So, using the excuse that he should wait for him on Planet Brymrr, Jest left, never to return.
When Baldy learned he had died, he wept and chose to seal himself away, using the passage of time to learn and keep growing until they met again.
In past eras, he had protected Planet Brymrr from all threats.
Now, he had returned to Kent’s side, still as a child but with overwhelming prowess.

Kent planned to spend some time with him, but before that, he wanted to have a clear idea of the spear he seized from Warlord Briana, the broken sword he bought at the auction, the Spirit Brush, and see where the path led next.
His wives informed him that they were taking Princess Luciana home, so he would be using the time he had to handle these issues.
Gaia had also informed him that they were done with 95% of the portal, so it wouldn’t be long before he was ready to head to Elina’s galaxy.
He brought out the spear and made it hover before him.
It seemed to have been made from a material that, to Kent, appeared like a stone and a bit like metal.
Given the texture, it would be a bit rough on the palm when wielded.
It was exactly 2 meters long, and one end was razor-sharp and scaly.
Nine runes have been carved on its length.
"Good spear, though I see nothing special about it that would suggest why that demon king was eager to get it." Kent focused more on the runes on it but saw nothing special.
It was ordinary at best; however, he knew it was in no way a simple spear.
If anything, the feeling of dread he felt when Warlord Biana activated one of the runes on it told him the spear was a terrifying weapon and that he should be careful around it.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
"Tower, what do you have on this weapon?" Since he was making no progress, he turned to Tower, who seemed to know most things that he did not.
Unfortunately, no good answer came from the tower.
However, she managed to give him something to go on.
[Regretfully, I have no idea what this spear is or where it came from.
However, there is a way the Master can find out.]
"I am all ears, Tower."
[Although I have no idea what the spear is, I can tell it is a soul weapon, meaning it has a soul space.
The Master can send a part of his consciousness inside and inspect it from within.
It isn’t linked to anyone, so there will be no defenses to break.
If that yields no results, then we can save it for now and look for answers later.]
Kent saw no problem with that.
He inhaled deeply and then exhaled.
He formed a hand seal and sent a strange part of his soul toward the spear.
He held his breath, watching as the strand of soul essence drifted toward the spear.
For a moment, he expected nothing to happen, but it did.
When it happened, he wasn’t prepared.

Just when his soul essence was close to the weapon, something took hold of it, and his entire soul was dragged into the spear, causing his body to fall backward and his soul to start falling into a dark hole.
Panic set in and was soon replaced by fear before he started to curse his life away.
In a span of what felt like eternity, Kent cursed his bad luck several hundred times.
But then he didn’t go splat.
Instead, he suddenly found himself standing in a large hall, its walls painted in ten different shades of color.
Kent took a deep breath and began examining his body.
After a few minutes, he stopped and let out a relieved sigh.
He was fine from head to toe, at least as far as his soul is concerned.
Once that was taken care of, he started to look around.
On the walls, he saw some writings, each with a background in a different color.
He moved closer to the one with a green background.
However, just when he was right before it, he found himself back to where he was.
"Hmmm, that is strange," Kent said, and then he moved again, stopping just where he had been before.
However, to his shock, it happened again.
"What in the hell is happening?" He tried three more times, but the same result.
So he switched to the blue wall and walked toward it.
But then the same thing happened.
He moved toward the red and three other colors, but the same thing happened.
Finally, Kent turned toward the golden color.
He chose this because something clicked in his mind that he may have overlooked.
When Warlord Biana used her life force to ignite the rune, it glowed golden.
Now, as he faced the golden wall, Kent hoped with every fiber of his being that he was right, or else he would go mad.
He took one step at a time, and before long, he was standing before the golden wall.
He closed his eyes and exhaled, knowing the moment he opened them, he would be back at the center of the hall.
"Well then..."
He snapped them open, and his gaze landed on the golden wall.
Instead of staring at it from ten meters away, he was looking at it from less than a meter away.
This caused him to blink a few times.
The next moment, however, the wall began to change as several writings appeared on it.
He lifted his head and looked at the header, and it read...
"Here lies the monument of Vael’Zhor, the Zodiac Forgebinder, creator and forger of the Sunfang Tyrant Spear, one of the ten Divine Zodiac Spears."
Kent blinked once or twice, his mind spinning as he read the header of the writing.
There were additional writings after the header; however, he couldn’t look past it.
He blinked again and read the header once more.
Then he turned and began reading the texts that followed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1539: Sunfang Tyrant Spear
paragraphs: "Every great blacksmith aspires to leave a legacy, one that will remain in their name even when they are long gone. Many came and went, and those who left a legacy are still remembered even after several eras.
Here lies the legacy of Vael’Zhor, the Zodiac Forgebinder, the one who aspired to forge the Zodiac Annihilation Formation.

This great hall holds the legacy of the Ten Divine Zodiac Spears. Whoever lays their gaze here is destined to walk the path of the 12 Zodiacs, assembling the ten spears and seeking the Heart and Mind of the Zodiac.
This is the legacy of Leo – Sunfang Tyrant Spear. Place your hand on the monument and receive the mark of Leo, becoming the master of the Sunfang Tyrant Spear."

Kent closed his eyes for a few moments, his mind spinning as he reeled in his thoughts. Just reading the inscriptions on the golden monument made him feel as if he had laid eyes on something forbidden.
The profundity of it all made him feel as though there was so much hidden from him.
However, he understood some things, and that made him happy.
With him having the name of the blacksmith who had forged this spear, he knew he could find out more information about them later.
He, after all, planned to join the cult of wisdom, so he would get to learn more about him later.
’Vael’Zhor, The Zodiac Forgebinder... what a peculiar name.’
His name is indeed peculiar.

Kent came from Earth, so he is familiar with the Zodiacs. He had researched those symbols, and hearing that there had once been a legendary blacksmith who went by such a name made him wonder just what all of this meant.

’Gather all ten spears... Heart and Mind... Zodiac Annihilation Formation... Just what are all these, and how would they help me in the long run?’ Kent said inwardly, his eyes opening slightly to behold the monument once more.
He sent a transmission to the tower, so he knew he wasn’t the only one there. The tower was there with him, and she had read the content as well, and thankfully, she had some answers for him.

[The master must know he is in the presence of greatness. The Zodiac Forgebinder was a legendary blacksmith who lived during the Flame Era. In fact, he was a member of the 13 Elder Blacksmiths, a council that even the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith was a part of.

I didn’t recognize the spear before because I had no memories of its contents. However, now that I know who created it, the master should know that the creator was someone whose name alone once shook many galaxies.

The Zodiac Forgebinder was the wielder of the Twelve Zodiac Flames, one of the sacred flames. He created many weapons and artifacts in his day; however, his greatest creation was the Zodiac Annihilation Formation.]
"Sounds like a powerful thing. Care to shed more light on it?" Kent said, looking at the heading of the inscriptions on the monument.
Everything was written in an ancient language that he could translate because he had the Universal Enigma. Even so, all he saw were names and nothing to make sense of them.
Now he wanted to find out more about one of the names.

[The Zodiac Annihilation Formation was a legendary formation that showed its brilliance during the Flame War. The idea was simple: the Zodiac Forgebinder decided to imbue the core essence of the 12 Zodiac Divine Flames into 12 weapons and link them using the Ancient Star Map.

It took 3 million years and a lot of effort to forge all the weapons. He succeeded after many failures, and that was when the Zodiac Annihilation Formation was born. A Tier 100 formation with 10 layers, each spear acting as a layer.
Once deployed, it cannot be stopped until all 10 layers have been executed. It was only used once, but legend has it that when it was deployed, over a hundred Celestials fell to its might.

After the Flame War ended, nobody knew where all 10 spears had gone, nor did they have the faintest idea where the Heart and Mind of the formation had gone. The Zodiac Forgebinder was also never seen or heard from again.
Some say he is still alive, while others say he is dead. But I know one thing: while the master is not a spearman, merging with the spear is the most logical decision you would ever make.]
Kent had no reason to doubt the Tower’s words. He had already sensed the monstrous nature of the spear, and so he knew there was just no way he would let go of it.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
If he binds with it, there is a chance he will one day need it, and knowing this spear is Leo, as far as the Zodiacs are concerned, having some fire on his side would not be too bad.
"I do have some questions first," Kent said, and then he asked, "What is a Sacred Flame?"
In the span of two days, there had been two mentions of the Sacred Flame by two different people. The first was Uncle Drake, and now the Tower did too. So he needed answers.
[The master is already aware of the Nirvana Flames, right?]
"Yes, Tower. What about them?"

[Well, I may have failed to paint a clear picture for you before, but Sacred Flames are the various flames that came directly from the Primal Chaos. As you already know, all creation came from the primal chaos.

These flames are the same, and they transcend all else. An example is the Flames of Nirvana. While they appear to be different since there are nine of them, in the eye of the Primal Chaos, they are considered as one.
This makes them a Sacred Flame. This also means the Flames of Nirvana are a Sacred Flame, and so are thousands of other Primordial Flames out there.
Just as the Nirvana Flame is powerful, so are many others. The 12 divine zodiac flames are among the most powerful sacred flames.
The only problem, however, is that obtaining a Sacred Flame is considered impossible. Only a few were able to wield one, and one of them was the Zodiac Forgebinder.]
Kent smirked. "Looks like I must unlearn and relearn again. The more I grow, the more complex things get."

Up until today, he thought the Nirvana Flame was the peak of flames. Now, it appeared that wasn’t the case. While the Nirvana Flames may be somewhere at the top of the list, he had no idea just where they would actually be placed.
It felt like the trump card he was hoping to wield against his greatest enemies had just become ordinary.
But it shouldn’t be. This spear is made from a Sacred Flame, and since he is also a wielder of a Sacred Flame, who knows what power lies dormant, ready to be unleashed?
So without hesitation, Kent pressed his palm against the surface of the monument, and a golden light enveloped him.
On the outside, golden flames surrounded the spear, and before long, the rust was washed away, revealing a majestic spear that exuded a terrifying aura, causing great pressure to descend on Kent.
Kent gritted his teeth, enduring the pressure for a few minutes before it suddenly vanished.
Before him, a series of texts appeared.
[You have successfully bound with the Sunfang Tyrant Spear]
[You have unlocked a new skill: Solar Devour]
[Solar Devour]
[Rank: Supreme]
[Description: Using the Sunfang Tyrant Spear as a medium, summon the Sacred Flames of Leo, the golden Zodiac flame that burns with furious hunger. The longer it burns, the stronger it becomes.]

chapters.title: Chapter 1540: The Complex Map
paragraphs: "I suppose that is one more trump card down for my journey through the Star Gateway," Kent smiled, gazing at the golden spear hovering before him.
Now that he had bonded with it, he could tell it was indeed a very powerful spear.

While his soul flame is not a Zodiac Flame, he could still feel some connection to it and knew that if he were to channel his own flame essence into it, then he would find a good medium to unleash all kinds of attacks.
Even better, he can tell his nirvana flames will come in handy now that he has a weapon forged from a sacred flame.
Right now, his flame element has only two techniques linked to it: the [Finger of Destruction] and [Divine Flame Armament].

While both are deadly techniques, he can use them only a few times before his two flame cores are drained. In fact, he can’t use them effectively in close combat, so he needed a way to use his flame for more controlled attacks.
The spear will do. He can unleash more managed attacks using both the Nirvana Flame and his soul flame.
"This also means I should take spear lessons from Neomi or Camilla."
He is a good swordsman, so maybe wielding the spear will be easy for him. Even so, having the chance to spend some quality time with his two wives won’t be too bad.
He grabbed the spear and examined it a few times before putting it away. It appeared inside his soul sea and hovered just before the first flame core.
Kent reached into the tower storage and pulled out the [Spirit Brush].
Looking at the knife-like item in his hand, a pale smile formed on his face. "Though not a soul item, it will make things much easier for me when painting."
He channeled his soul energy into it, and at once it transformed into a sleek-looking paintbrush. Kent, who had used many spirit brushes in the past, smiled and tapped into that knowledge.
He activated the brush’s many forms, causing it to change from one design to another for a couple of seconds before returning to its knife form.
"Since I will be facing immortal-level threats on my way to Elina’s galaxy, I must also have immortal-level paintings on my side," he smiled and tapped into the memories of Jest.
Having lived a full life in that incarnation, he had seen and experienced a great deal. This meant he had more to paint and fewer forbidden words to inscribe.
While most would be dangerous to paint, if he managed to get a few done, then his journey would be a lot less harrowing.
After examining the spirit brush for a few more seconds, he exhaled and put it away. Then he retrieved the map he had purchased at the auction.

It was worn out, with holes riddling some portions of it. However, the diagram on it is very valuable, so valuable that even gods will kill to learn it. Unfortunately for them, they had no way to decipher it, so it is now Kent’s turn to try his hand at it.
"Tower, extract and project the diagram in a digital form."
The map flew from his hand and hovered for a few seconds before the complex diagram on it rose and expanded, taking up the three-foot space before him.
Kent stood up and calmly examined it. Deep in his subconscious, a nerd slowly started to awaken the longer he studied the diagram.
"Hmm, this seems like those complex encryptions I learned during my master’s degree back on Earth," Kent smirked and continued to look.

The diagram contained a single node that held the Hexa-Spiral 360 Paradox Grid. However, the person who drew the map seemed too smart—and a bit wicked—to have encrypted the main enigma behind another complex pattern schema called the Voidscript 888 Recursive Pattern.

Right now, Kent would have to isolate all useless patterns from the main diagram and then decipher the main node using the Voidscript 888 Recursive Pattern before he would be able to see the patterns that he had to decrypt to find the locations of the treasures left behind by that legendary blacksmith.
For now, however, he allowed himself to be immersed in the thrill of the complex computations he would be diving into.
An hour later, he seemed to have grasped the core concept of the diagram.
His hands moved, and patterns flew out of the main diagram. Soon, only a triangular shape was left. Kent looked at it for a few more seconds and then smiled.
"Oh, the brain behind this map is plenty smart, all right." He saw that to handle this triangle, he must immerse himself in learning more about the Voidscript 888 Recursive Pattern.
He is smart, but he seems to still be lacking. Perhaps his lack had to do with still not having his memories of Kevin Sage back.

"Tower, buy all books and manuscripts on all kinds of ancient cryptographic algorithms out there. I want everything from the dawn of time to this very moment." A pale smile appeared on his face. "I guess it is time to hit the books again."
[I will do as the master says. But I first have to let Gaia build a sizable library to store everything.]
Kent laughed.

Perhaps if he were to recover his memories of Kevin Sage, solving the pattern would be simple. However, since he had yet to have that knowledge, acquiring it on his own for now seemed like a good thing.
"I might end up not needing it in the end, but for now, having a library would add to the beauty of the place."
He let the Tower save the extracted triangular pattern. For now, he would end things there and continue later.
The last thing he wanted was to become absorbed in this and neglect his preparation for the mission coming up in a few months.
After stowing everything away, his focus turned to the last item he had bought at the auction house. The moment the broken sword appeared, Gaap emerged from his soul sea as well.

Aside from him sensing the resentful qi coming from the sword when he saw it, Gaap was also attracted to it, and so he went ahead and lied through his teeth, claiming he planned on buying it as an antique when, in fact, he knew the broken sword was something extremely powerful.
"I don’t suppose you have any idea what this sword was before it broke?" Kent asked, but Gaap shook his head. He moved closer to get a better look at it.

"I can clearly sense a very potent resentment coming from within; however, I can’t figure out how to access it." Gaap narrowed his eyes at the broken sword, his gaze drifting along the wooden hilt, paying close attention to the markings on it.
"Same here."

At the auction, they claimed there is a supreme-grade technique for cultivating sword aura hidden inside this sword. However, Kent knew they were lying. But despite calling their bluff, he also could not make sense of what was rooted deep inside the sword.
Maybe if he were the only one who sensed it, he would have doubted himself. However, he, the Tower, and Gaap all sensed it, and so he knew the sword was a treasure.
But even after four hours of examining and trying all kinds of harmless experiments, nothing happened. In the end, it came down to one final method.
"I suppose feeding it my blood would be the last thing to try. Already, I couldn’t send my consciousness inside, and neither could you, so let me try that."
Gaap looked at Kent for a few seconds before nodding.
"Be careful, though. While we have no idea what this sword is, the fact that it could scare someone like me shows it is a terrifying weapon."
Kent nodded, and then, after a sigh, he cut his palm and let his blood drip onto the hilt of the broken sword.
